Sub: Forwarding of Training Calendar of 2016-17 & seeking for fresh Training Profile on
the eve of new session of 2016-17 — reg.

Sir / Madam,

The Training Calendar for the year 2016-17 as approved by NATRSS, New Delhi
is enclosed herewith for your Kind perusal and necessary action.

In this context, it is requested to kindly keep in mind the following points while
following while sponsoring the Staff members/Officers (up to Group ‘B’) to any of the
Training Programmes (TPs):

1. Nominating Officials for TPs by ZTI: First, as you may be aware, Zonal Training
Institute, East Zone, Kolkata, as per directions of NATRSS and HO, has been
selecting/nominating names of Officials for various Training Programmes (TPs), since
September, 2013 based on the Training Profiles received from respective ROs and SROs
(except Orissa Region).

However, there are constraints faced by ZTI in making nominations owing to nonreceipt of up-to-date position / status of all the staff members / Officers (up to Group-

‘B’), i.e., their transfer/ posting / promotion / resignation / retirement, etc. either in time

or not at all.

It is, therefore, requested to please send a copy of the order of all the
transfer-posting / promotion / resignation / retirement etc. whenever the

same happens to update the Training Profile at this end.

Sponsoring Participants by ROs/SROs: First, even though, Zonal Training Institute,

East Zone, Kolkata, as per directions of NATRSS and HO, has been selecting names of
Officials for various Training Programmes (TPs), ROs and SOs since September, 2013
based on the Training Profiles received from all the field Offices (except Orissa Region),
are free to amend or alter the list of nominees and substitute other officials in the

List of Participants under situations as follows:

A. Any official nominated for a specific TP has already undergone the training earlier;

B. There are other officials who require the specific TP more than the ones selected;

C. There are officials who have not undergone any training whatsoever since more
than one year;

D. Due to pressing urgency or exigencies, official/officials nominated for a specific TP
cannot be spared;

E. Officials nominated cannot come for training due to their personal difficulties which
up to the judgment of OICs concerned may be genuine enough to spare them from

a specific TP.

ing the Training Profiles of Officials ROs/SROs: Updated Training
Profiles are required to assess the training needs of officials. Training Profiles are
awaited from some of the field offices.

All the OICs are, therefore, requested to kindly send the Training Profiles of all their
Officials / Officers (up to Group-'B’) updating their profiles up to March, 2016
in the proforma as given below for smooth functioning of the Training Programmes

Subject: Functioning of field offices on 02" April 2016 for upload and
reconciliation of the challans.

Sir/Madam,

It has been experienced that there have been issues from the SBI side in providing
the complete entries in e-Challans from December 2015 onwards due to which the upload
and reconciliation of Challans has been getting delayed in EPFO.

2s Many steps were taken by NDC to resolve the issues. All the e-Challan files were got
regenerated at SBI at the end of every month and after receiving the regenerated files the
e-Challans available with field offices were compared with the regenerated files and new
entries in the regenerated files were provided to the field offices as part e-Challans files.
Nearly 1.5 Lakh e-Challans were provided to the field offices for each of the month.
However as on date there are Challans that are pending for upload and reconciliation in the
application software, majority of which belong to March 2016.

3. If these e-Challans remain pending for upload and reconciliation it will have an
advance impact on the annual interest crediting. In order to credit the contributions of these
e-Challans in the member accounts and credit the interest on these contributions during the
annual interest processing it is mandatory to get these pending e-Challans uploaded and
reconciled before the annual interest processing.

4. The part files for the period 01% March-20" March 2016 were provided to the field
offices so that the work of part e-Challans gets minimized at the end of the month. SBI is
being asked to regenerate e-Challans for the complete month of March 2016 on 1* April
2016. NDC will provide the left over part e-Challans for the March 2016 on 2™ April which
needs to be uploaded and reconciled on the same day itself. It is therefore decided that all
the field offices will remain open and functional on 2™ April 2016 for the upload and
reconciliation of the part e-Challans.

5. To re-generate part e-Challans it is to be ensured esi the e-Challan files already
available with field office are uploaded by 31.03.2016 after which MIS Group 3 data is to be
generated and provided to NDC without fail at the end of the 31.03.2016. It is to be further
ensured by the field offices that no Challan remains pending to be uploaded after the
generation of MIS Group 3 data on 31.03.2016. On 2™ April 2016 NDC will provide part eChallan file which should be uploaded and reconciled before annual account processing.
After upload of these part e-Challans daily upload and reconciliation of e-Challans may be
resumed.

6. The following points are being reiterated:

(a) Field offices to remain open on 2™ April 2016 for upload and reconciliation of eChallans.

(b) All the available Challans to be uploaded and reconciled by 31.03.2016.

(c) MIS Group 3 to be generated on 31.03.2016 (5.30 P.M.) and provided to NDC.
(d) No Challans to be uploaded after generation of MIS Group 3 on 31.03.2016

(e) Part e-Challan file to be provided by NDC on 02 April 2016 which needs to be
uploaded and reconciled.

(f) After upload of e-Challan file provided on 02" April 2016 daily upload and
reconciliation of Challans may be resumed.

7. This issues with the approval of Central Provident Fund Commissioner.

Yours faithfully

Sub: Coverage of Banks-regarding;
Sir,

In exercise of the powers conferred by clause (b) of Sub-Section (3) of Section 1 read with
Section 16 of the EPF & MP Act, 1952 the Central Government has notified that the Act shall apply to
all banks employing 20 and more number of persons as a class of establishment in respect of those
employees who are not entitled to the benefit of Contributory Provident Fund or old age pension in
accordance with any Scheme or rule framed by the Central Government or the State Government or
by the respective banks established under the Banking Regulations Act, 1949 (10 of 1949). In this
regard the Notification issued by Ministry of Labour & Employment having number S.O. 444 (E)
issued on 10" Feb., 2016 is enclosed. As such all banks shall be covered from the date of notification
i.e. 10.02.2016. It is clarified that this notification shall cover all employees as per definition under
Section 2(f) of EPF & MP Act, 1952 excluding the employees who are getting benefits of PF and
Pension according to rules of concerned banks.

In view of the above, it is requested to take required steps to cover such establishments. A
proactive approach may be adopted and the establishments be provided guidance and help in
completing the registration formalities. The establishments may be guided about provisions of the Act
and Schemes and the responsibilities of the employers. The allotment of UANs to the employees
covered, their activation and seeding with KYC norms be ensured simultaneously,

Subject:
Time bound completion of data entries in HR software and test run of modules -reg.
Sir/Madam,
You are well aware that HR Software have been developled for the purpose of uploading the Service
particulars of each of the officers/officials by NDC/IS Division on the following subject:
i.
HRPIS New Function: Incumbency Report of OIC in the HR software.
ii.
HRPIS New Function: Generation of EID for the EPF employee pensioners.
iii.
Data Entry of sanctioned strength in the HR software.
2.
To operate the above software instructions have already been issued vide this office circular dated
02.12.2015. The purpose for this software was that once the data entered initially, thereafter on any change in
the status of an employee whether by way of promotion/transfer/deputation/leaving service etc. The data will
be updated so that all the reports are correctly displayed and also the e-service book part is uploaded
authomatically.
3.
On going through the random check-up of the data after the recent transfer has shown that while most
of the officer are updating the data in similar cases officer of upto the RPFC-II level are still reflected in the
old offices with old designation. This check was done for the ACC & RPFC-1 and II level officers.
4
It is also to inform that the data entry in the software was strictly as per certified Input Data Sheets
where the data was either provided by the Employee (personal details), or by Admin Section in the office
(Service Book details). User Manuals for each function is already made available in the software itself. The email id of hr.softwareäepfinida.gov.in has been provided for any query of reporting any issue. However it is
seen that some HR users are experimenting with the software.
5.
The CPFC was recently apprised of the initiative but he expressed his anguish on the adherence to the
various time lines of data entry and test run of the modules. It is therefore incumbent upon all the supervisory
offices to see that these tasks are completed in time. The successful completion of the modules will enable the
futher introduction of new modules to improve HR functions like auto generation of salary, APAR entry
updation, leave entries, calculation of vacancies, vigilance profile, creation of individual employee login.

--
6.
In view of the above all the Regional Commissioners, and Officer-Incharge of RO/SRO are
requested to take necessary action on the following points strictly:-
I. Update the posting of all the employees.
ii. Advise the users, to go through the user manual before using any function.
7.
It has been further decided that Addl. CPFC zones shall monitor the progress in respect of the
offices under the zones by suitably identifying a Nodal Officer. They will monitor progress at regular intervals.
8.
If there is any inconvience is being felt in feeding of data, help of the user manual of each function
is available under the HELP menu for every HR soft user. In case of any clarification, they can write at
hr.software P ep find ia.gov.in and/or rc.nd(äepfindia.gov.in .

Subject : Launching of Salary Module in the HRSoft ( Software for HR Management) - completion
of data entry and testing - reg.
Madam! Sir,
Please refer to this office letter no. CAT. 22(17)2015/HQ dated 14.01.2016 ( website SI No.
617/2015-16) vide which it was intimated that the module for preparation of Salary from the
HRSOFT is under development and that the trial run at five offices namely RO, Delhi (South)
Madural, Peenya and SROs KR Puram and Laxminagar is to be done for testing.
2.
While reviewing the progress of the same, the Central PF Commissioner has directed that
the salary module of HRSOFT should be launched on 29.03.2016 in the CBT Meeting and that the
salary for the month of April 2016 shall be generated only from this module in all the offices of
E P FO.
3.
In order to achieve this timeline, the following urgent action has to be taken by all the field
offices
(i)
Ensure that all the employees who have been working in their respective offices
since October 2015 should be updated included subsequent changes in posting / station / cadre etc
in the personal profile of all employees.
(ii)
Ensure that all the employees currently posted in each office should have EID and
their SPF details and PAN Number should be entered. Thus the following fields in respect of each
and every employee working since October 2015 (All cadres) should be filled in:-
a.
PAN
b.
SPF/PRAN
c.
Bank Account details
(iii)
A downloadable (xIs file) has been provided through the salary software,
(Add/Check Bank Account function). This file has the list of all EIDs with name and designation of
presently posted employees in the office. This file can be used for linking each employee from the

current salary software used by the office as the names may have been different typed. Thereafter,
all upload will be based on EID. This list will also help you in finding such employees who are
presently posted in your office but not listed in downloaded (.xls file). This may be because of the
EID not generated or the said employee shown under different. Immediate action should be taken
for.
(iv)
Technical persons in each office to be associated with the activity to ensure speedy
resolution of any problems.
(v)
Any issues / problems arising should be taken up with NDC immediately as per
procedure already laid down for HRSoft.
(vi)
All offices should complete the above data feeding and authenticate the same by
31.03.2016 without fail.
(vii)
All field offices should complete the preparation for the implementation of the
Salary Module of HRSOFT by 05.04.2016 without fail and compare the salary generated by software
and that already paid to ensure that the two should tally. After the bank related details are
uploaded, the salary file for October, 2015 should be uploaded. The format for this has been made
available. There are two formats. However, the (.csv) format should be used for faster upload.
Thereafter, no upload is required and the salary can be generated for subsequent months through
Generate Salary function and necessary changes such as adding or removing employee can be as per
actuals. The user manual is already available in HELP menu in HR Software.
(viii)
Any difference in the two (local software and HR Software) should be examined to
ensure that there is no data entry error in the module and only then referred to NDC for
examination.
(ix)
It is also advised to use a broadband connection with a reasonable speed such as 2
mbps for uploading and processing the data. Step by step process already available in user manual
is enclosed for reference.
(x)
The action taken by Delhi (South) and ASD shall be directly monitored and studied
by RPFC(NDC) as field testing of the module. As already intimated, issues and guidelines if any
required may please be taken up with the team at NDC through email rc.ndc@epfindia.gov.in ,
hr.software@epfindia.gov.in .
Yours faithfully,

SOCIAL SECURITY AGREEMENT WITH THE REPUBLIC OF AUSTRALIA
_——eaexeeNrvw sve we NF} THE REPUBLIC OF AUSTRALIA

The Government of India has entered into an Agreement on Social Security
Agreement with Australia. Following the principles of reciprocity this, agreement
is intended to benefit the employees of both India as well as the Australia. The
agreement has come into force w.e.f 01-01-2016

The Agreement provides inter-alia for posting i.e. detachment up to a
period of 60 months for employees of both the countries. Accordingly the
employees of one country deputed by their employers to the other country on
short-term assignment for a pre-determined period of up to a period of 60
months need not remit Social Security Contributions in that country. Thus the
employers are saved from making double Social Security contributions for the
same set of employees thereby enhancing the competitiveness of their products
and services.

Employees’ Provident Fund Organization (EPFO) has been identified as the
agency of implement the provisions of the agreement in India and has been
authorized to issue “Certificate of coverage” to the employees of Indian
establishment posted to the Australia.

The employers, who have already deputed/intend to depute their
employees to the Australia can avail of this facility. The application form for this
purpose is available on the official web site http://www.epfindia.gov.in. The
“Certificate of coverage” will be issued by concerned RO/SRO where the
application is submitted. They may also contact their jurisdictional Regional
Provident Fund Commissioner or the International Workers Unit in the Head
Office at 14, Bhaikaji Cama Place, New Delhi -110066 for any further details

mounting on one hand and recovery thereof shows a downwards trend which is very
much alarming.

While going through the details of Current Demand and Arrear Demand (UnExempted and Exempted) for the month of January, 2016, it has come to notice that

(Mumbai - II), Kolkata and Chennai Regions have performed, not so well in Current
Demand (Un-Exempted and Exempted). All the above said eleven Regions have not
achieved the target of 100% recovery as already set by Head Office in the area of
recovery of Current Demand.

Further, in Arrear Demand (Un-Exempted and Exempted) category,
performance of Bandra, Ranchi, Bhubaneswar, Indore, and Delhi(South), Pune,
Chandigarh, Dehradun, Meerut and Delhi (North) Regions is not upto the mark.

In addition to above, it is observed that performance of Delhi (South), Ranchi
and Chandigarh Regions needs to be improved in both Current Demand and Arrear
Demand.

Sub: Timely Seeding of KYC Data in UAN — reg;
Madam /Sir, .

The allotment of UAN and its accompanying facilities like portability, updated
balances etc. have reformed the service delivery mechanism of EPFO. In this connection it is
imperative to ensure that all UAN’s allotted are seeded with KYCs by employers and all the
members. The KYCs mandatory to be seeded in the UAN database of a member for portability
are his Bank Account and either Aadhar or PAN. There is need for special focused drive to
seed the UAN of currently active members. An analysis of the details available on UAN shows
that out of 3,06,36,276 UANs allotted to the contributing members, Bank account is available in
respect of 1,50,80,936 UANs. Where the Bank account with either Aadhar/PAN is available in
such cases seeding stands completed. Based on the above analysis, three distinct works are
identified for the field offices as below:-

1. Cases where Bank details are available, seeding of these 51,17,900 UANs is to be
completed by obtaining either Aadhar or PAN.

2. Cases where either Aadhar/PAN is available but Bank account is not available. In these
16,19,783 cases, Bank account details are to be collected and seeded.

3. Cases where no details are available, their Bank account is to be collected and seeded
with Aadhar or PAN in 1,49,91,753 UANs.

The Office wise i.e Regional Office/Sub-Regional Office details where the afore
mentioned seeding is required as on 11.03.2016 for each of the above mentioned categories is
made available by CAIU-Compliance Wing at MIS portal download- UAN data-CAIU.

RO/SROs can mail this list of employees as stated above vide 1, 2 & 3 to
establishments to complete the seeding and subsequently depute an official to facilitate it.
Whenever an EO is scheduled to visit an establishment, the list of employees whose Bank
account/Aadhar/PAN details are not available can be sent in advance to that establishment with
request to keep the details ready. The assistance of DEO may be provided to EO to provide
technical assistance to facilitate this. The seeding of UAN with KYC as per the lists available on

MIS portal download- UAN data- CAIU needs to be completed 100% by 15/04/2016 and
officials other than EOs can also be authorised for this work.

Further the work related to the digital signatures which is already made mandatory
for all the establishments vide order no. Coord/40(24)2010/DPG/Review Meeting/ Dated
11/12/2015 and the last date for which was 31/12/2015 also needs to be completed alongside.
It is also observed that a large no. of KYC details have been uploaded but the same have not
been verified by the employers using digital signature. This needs to be taken up with
establishments.

RC-I of the Region is to achieve this target with the help of RC (F&A) & RC (C&R).
Intensive effects need to be put in to achieve the results by engaging all the stakeholders.
Zonal ACCs are requested to monitor the progress of aforementioned tasks in respect of each
of the offices under their jurisdiction and ensure timely completion of the task attaching the
highest priority to this activity.

Yours faithfully,

Subject: Implementation of CCPAP for cheques drawn on A/C no. 2 w.e.f. March 10, 2016.
Reference: Circulars at Serial numbers 434 and 698 on EPFO website under circular section for
the year 2015-16.

Madam /Sir,
As we all are aware, to improve safety, cheques drawn on A/C no. 1, 10, and 21 are migrated to
a payment platform known as Corporate Cheque Drawn at Par (CCPAP). Now this system is to
be extended to cover cheques drawn on A/C no. 2 and the date for its implementation, as
communicated earlier, is March 10, 2016. Items of preparatory work, which were supposed to
be complete at the level of RO/SRO concerned, for this rollout are listed below:
1. Each office must get existing/old A/C 2 closed and should get a new bank account
(current account) for A/C 2 opened under CCPAP category.
2. All old A/C 2 cheques (Instrument type 11) must be disposed of as per extant
instructions.
3. New instrument (cheque books) namely, “Multicity (Payable at par) CTS-2010 Standard
Cheques” (MCC), (Instrument type 29) must be secured from the relevant bank branch
(all Core Banking branches are authorized to issue MCCs).
4. Digital signatures to be secured for DDO alongwith two link officers alongwith
completion of related paraphernalia.
5. WAR software supplement released recently by the Project Division for this purpose has
to be installed and integrated with the present system software.

Regarding timeline, new CCPAP-enabled current account A/C 2 was to be opened and MCC
cheques secured against newly opened account on or before December 10, 2015 i.e. a minimum
of three months prior to the proposed rollout date. Completion of the listed actions three
months in advance is necessitated to ensure that no old A/C 2 cheque drawn on earlier saving
A/C 2 which are within their validity period (within 3 months from the date of issue) and yet to
be encashed are dishonoured on account of closure of the old saving A/C no. 2.

Accordingly, all officers are required to ensure that starting March 10, 2016, all cheques
drawn on A/C 2 are issued through CCPAP platform.

This issues with the approval of Regional Commissioner-I (F&A).

Yours faithfully

(Sudarshan Kumar)

Sub: - Coverage of contact workers under EPF & MP Act, 1952 — reg.
Madam/Sir,

The issue of coverage of contract workers has been flagged as an area of top most concern
and priority by the Government of India. Number of instructions have been issued by EPFO Head
Office in recent past to ensure that all eligible workers are brought under the ambit of EPF & MP
Act, 1952. The action plan has hitherto been to ensure that

(a) All the agencies and contractors to whom the work is outsourced are covered under the Act;

(b) All the personnel supplied by the agencies and contractors are extended benefits of
provident fund etc; and

(c) All the personnel engaged get eligible benefits commensurate to the wage they get.

Considering that our aim is to reach out to the last employee, the data collection from
different sources itself requires serious and constant efforts. In this endeavor to collect the
intelligent and actionable information, to facilitate the work of field offices, a software has been
developed through which a login has been provided to both the category of establishments-principal
employers- those which are registered with EPFO and those which are not registered with EPFO like
the Government Departments. After authentication through One Time Password (OTP), the principal
employer can enter details of contractor and work order, which will be segregated PIN code wise
and will go to the respective portal of SRO/RO and can be viewed online, as and when updated.

When this information is uploaded in the system, CAIU, HO shall have the option to view it
while this shall originally be reflected in the login of the RO/SRO. The RO/SRO can verify with the
respective database of covered establishments whether the particular contactor establishments is
already registered and its compliance position. There after RO/SRO can decide/shall have option

(a) To allocate inspection to particular inspector
(b) Define time limits for inspection

(c) Option for uploading of reports in particular format

(d) Reason for late uploading of reports

(e) Reason for Pendency in uploading of reports

(f) Coverage status of establishment (Already Covered, New Coverage)

(g) No. of new employees covered if any

(h) Remarks/Comments by APFC/RPFC-II to indicate the satisfaction level of report.

(i) In case the satisfaction level is below certain limit, inspection has to redone and reports
to be uploaded again by EO.

At this instant the Head Office is not making any intervention/giving remarks or obervations
after the work order is uploaded by the principal employer. The field offices need to check
compliance under the EPF & MP Act, 1952 vis-a-vis the individual work orders in the back drop of
office records available and decide if inspection is required. In case inspection is deemed required,
separate permission may be sought from CAIU giving details as per the instructions already invouge
for seeking permission for inspection.

CAIU, HO shall monitor the performance of RO/SRO and have the option to provide its own
remarks/directions subsquently.

CPFC has already written DO letters to major Principal employers to avail this facility and it is
possible that some of them might contact you in this regard.

In view of the above, all the Regional PF commissioners, Incharge of Regional & Sub
Regional Offices are advised to ensure that this facility is properly utilized and to ensure that all
eligible workers working though contractors are enrolled. The facility is available through official
website of EPFO (http://www.epfindia.gov.in >For Employers >For Principal Employers) or at

http://www.epfindia.com/site_en/Principal Employer.php. The individual login id for . respective
Offices shall be mailed shortly.

For any technical clarification Shri Dinesh Dharni, Deputy Director (IS) and Shri Randhir
Kumar, APFC (CAIU) may be contacted at Telephone No. 011/26163245 dk.dharni@epfindia.gov.in
and 011/26714171 email id randhir.kumar@epfindia.gov.in respectively .

Yours faithfully,

(M. Narayanappa)

Sub: Supply of information under Right to Information Act, 2005 - reg.

Sir,

Please find enclosed herewith a letter of Sh. Shakti H., received in this office on 02.03.2016, for
seeking information under the Right to Information Act. The Copy of the letter is forwarded to you for
necessary action under the Right to Information Act, 2005. The information has to be provided directly to
the applicant under intimation to the undersigned. It is certified that the applicant has deposited the
application fee ie. Rs.10/-

If the desired information does not pertain to the concerned division or some part of information
is held by other division or public authority, the concerned CPIO shall forward /transfer the application
or such Part of it as may be appropriate to relevant division/Public authorities u/s 5(4) and 6(3) of the
RTI Act, 2005 respectively and inform the applicant immediately /about such transfer. However, if the
CPIO is not able to find out as to which division/public authority is concerned with the information even
after making reasonable efforts to find out the concerned division/public authority to which the
application could be transferred. It would, however, be the responsibility of the CPIO, if an appeal is made
against his decision, to establish that he made reasonable efforts to find out the particulars of the
concerned division/ public authority.

If some part of the information is the concern of a public authority under any State Government
or the Union Territory Administration, the CPIO receiving the application should inform the applicant that

Subject: Special Recovery Drive during the month of March,2016.

Sir,

The increasing trend of arrears of Provident Fund and allied dues has become a
matter of great concern. So much so, the performance in recovery of current and arrear
dues is far below the targets fixed by the Headquarters.

2. The all India Performance for the previous year upto December, 2015 as per

Annual Business Plan establishes the fact that there is urgent need to take further legal

actions, and closely moniter the same in pursuit to achive the targets in time bound

manner.

c# In order to augment recovery, it has been decided that a Special Recovery Drive

is carried out during the month of March, 2016 (for both un-exempted and exempted

sector).

4, Instructions issued vide this office letters dated, 19.06.2012 (placed at S.No. 187

at website), dated 13.07.2012 (placed at S.No.221 at website), dated 01.10.2013

(placed at S. No. 411 at website), dated 10.1.2014 (placed at S.No. 647 at website and

dated 28.05.2014 (placed at S.No. 160 at website), dated 03.02.2015 (placed at S.

No.746 at website) and dated 14.07.2015 (placed at S.No.243 at website) should be

adhered to scrupulously.

5. The following points shall be kept in mind while conducting the Special Recovery

Drive:

a) Maximum number of Enforcement Officers, as far as practicable, shall be detailed
to carry out such drive without disturbing other functional areas. The Enforcement
Officers before proceeding in the matter shall gather all information viz. details of
bank accounts, details of sundry debtors etc. from the records available in the
office and also from third party source like Income Tax Department, Inspector of
Factories and Boilers’, Inspector of Shops and Establishments, Employees’ State
Insurance Corporation, Regional Transport Authorities, Industries and Commerce
Departments, Industrial Estates, Local Bodies, Co-operative Department, Director
of Mining and Geology, Employers’ Associations, Trade Unions etc.

-2b) RPFCs In-charge of Regional Offices/Sub Regional Offices shall closely
monitor the progress of recovery during the currency of the drive on weekly
basis and action plan accordingly shall be prepared for the following week(s).

c) Vide publicity shall be given on such launching of the Special Recovery Drive
through local News Papers, display on the notice boards of the Office
prominently, through Employers’, Associations and Trade Unions.

d) The consolidated report regarding performance of the Regional Offices during
Special Recovery Drive - March, 2016 in respect of Current Demand and
Arrear Demand (Un-Exempted & Exempted) must be reported office wise by
the ACCs In-Charge of the zone in the enclosed Annexure for un-exempted
and exempted sector separately to Head Office by e-mail at
dir.recovery@epfindia.gov.in Please note that the consolidated report must
be received in Head Office by 04.04.2016 without fail.

e) Reports received from Regional Offices and Sub Regional Offices will not be

taken into cognizance.

f) It shall be noted that the amount outstanding as on 01.03.2016 shall be the
Opening Balance and recoveries made prior to 01.03.2016 shall not be
included with recoveries made during the recovery month.

g) It is further clarified that the figures reported during recovery month must be
the same as reported in ABP report which will be the monitoring report for the
performance of recovery. ;

6. The above actions are meant to be taken for meeting the objectives of speedy

recovery of dues and not for any harassment of the employers/defaulters, which

the RPFCs must ensure.

7. It is hoped that all out efforts shall be made to make the Special Recovery

Drive a success in its true spirit.

(This issues with the approval of Competent Authority).

Yours etal,

Sub:- Empanelment of Hospital and Diagnostic Centre's for medical treatment to the
retired employees of EPFO and their family - regarding.
Ref:- HRM-VIII/V/12(7)2007/Mumbai/31810 dated 03.12.2015.
Sir,
I am directed to invite a reference to Head Office letter dated 05.02.2009 and this office
letter of even No. dated 03.12.2015 calling for details of private hospitals empanelment by Zonal
Addl. CPFC.
2.
In this regard as per the input received from various Zonal Addl. CPFCs it has been
informed, that private Hospitals are not coming forward to accept the terms & conditions of
empanelment for extending cashless medical facility to EPFO retired employees and their
dependent family members and particularly some hospitals are not ready to provide bank
guarantee and earnest money even or to offer discount as per terms and conditions of draft
MOU circulated by Head Office with the Head Office circular date 05.02.2009.
3.
In view of the above, it has been decided to re-examine the instructions in order to
facilitate empanelment of more private hospitals for providing cashless medical facility to retired
Employees of EPFO and their dependent family.
4.
It is requested to forward your suggestions regarding changes required to be made in the
terms and conditions for empanelment of Hospitals circulated by Head Office within a period of
10 days and by 04.03.2016 positively.
Yours faithfully,
(Sanjay Bisht)
Regional P.F. Commissioner-I (HRM)

Sub: Delegation of financial/administrative powers in case of indoor
medical treatment taken by the retired employees of EPFO and/or
their spouse/dependents under CS (MA) Rules, 1944 - regarding.
Sir,
This is in regard to certain references received from various regions about
regulation of cases of indoor medical treatment taken by the retired employees of
EPFO and/or their spouse/dependents involving relaxation under CS(MA)
rules, 1944.In certain Regions, court cases have also been filed by retired employees
for medical reimbursement in case of indoor medical treatment taken by the them
and/or their spouse/dependents from non-recognized hospitals in emergent
circumstances.
2.
In this regard, attention is invited to HO circular no. HRIV1-V/12(2)2004/48740
dated 1.10.2009(copy enclosed) vide which it was clarified that delegation of
financial/administrative powers, in the case of indoor treatment taken by the retired
employees of EPFO and/or their spouse/dependents, are meant for cases involving
relaxation under CS (MA) Rules, 1944.Therefore, it is requested to regulate all such
cases accordingly to avoid inconvenience to the retired employees.
Yours faithfully,
(Sanjay Bish )
Regional P.F. Commissioner-I (HRM)

Subject: Recovery of Current and Arrear Demand for the period April -December
2015-Regarding.

Madam /Sir,

The performance of the field offices for recovery of dues for the period AprilDecember 2015 was reviewed. The following picture in this regard emerges.

1. Recovery of Current Demand (Un-exempted and Exempted)

(a) As per instructions contained in Head Office circular dated 19.06.2012
(available at S| No 187/2012 on the website), the targets set in the category of current
demand is 100 percent. This target is yet to be achieved as only 41.31% of the dues
have been recovered at the end of December 2015 for the country as a whole. Only
three offices namely Ahmedabad (86.74), Madurai (78.01) and Baroda (74.07) have
managed to cross the 70%.

The worst three performers in terms of percentage of Recovery are Patna
(12.29), Bangalore (15.77) and Raipur (17.40).

2. Recovery of Arrear Demand (Un-exempted and Exempted)

(a) As per instructions contained in Head Office circular dated 19.06.2012
(available at Sl No 187/2012 on the website), the targets set in the category of arrear
demand is 80 percent. This target is yet to be achieved as only 07.06% of the dues
have been recovered at the end of December 2015 for the country as a whole. Only
three offices namely Guwahati (31.08), Hyderabad (27.96) and Raipur (27.46) have
managed to cross the 25%.

The worst three performers in terms of percentage of Recovery are Mumbai-I
(0.48), Ranchi (0.78) and Bhubaneswar (1.76).

3. Recovery of Current Demand (Un-exempted) NIR

In the NIR category, it is seen that bulk of the amount (in lakhs) is locked with,
Kolkatta (5201.30), Jalpaiguri (4093.09), Chennai (2973.48), Nagpur (2266.89) and
Indore (2055.52).

4. Recovery of Current Demand (Exempted) NIR

In the NIR category, it is seen that bulk of the amount (in lakhs) is locked with Delhi
North (1595.57), Kolkatta (1485.24), and Raipur (900.22).

Low percentage of Recovery reveals that more closely, required legal actions has to be
taken and completed in time bound manner, so as to ensure to achieve the targets
prescribed thereupon.

As the financial year 2015-16 is coming to close soon, the recovery machinery has to
be re energised to achieve the targets so that consequent efficient services to the
members can be provided.

Similarly, all prescribed legal actions may also be taken in the sphere of Arrear
Demand(Un-Exempted & Exempted NIR) and convert the same as Realizable dues and
recover the same immediately.

Yours faithfully,

Dr. A. K. Dubey
Additional Central Provident Fund Commissioner (Recovery)

Sub: Guidelines for Quasi-judicial proceedings under Section 7A of the
Employees Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act 1952-regarding.

Madamn/Sir,

In continuation of Head Office Circular No.7 (1)2012/RCs R M dated 06.08.2014
on the above subject, the following instructions for conducting Quasi-judicial
proceedings under Section 7A are being issued.

The Executive Committee, CBT, EPF in its 82"! meeting held on 20" August,
2015 had directed to place the report of Committee constituted to examine and _ identify
the technical reasons where the Hon’ble Courts have passed orders against the EPFO
and suggest necessary corrective/remedial measures. A Committee constituted for the
purpose consisting of senior officers has broadly identified the following two reasons
related to Compliance regarding procedure to be adopted while conducting 7A enquiry
which lead to the adverse decision against the Department:

i. Denial of natural justice:
ii. Order passed by the adjudicating authority without proper justification -

Hence the authorized officers conducting the 7A inquiry are advised to strictly
adhere to the following norms of conducting 7A enquiry under the EPF & MP
Act, 1952:

a) Whenever a 7A inquiry is initiated, the basis for initiation of 7A inquiry such
as EO’s reports etc must be served to the establishment/employer.

b) It must be ensured that 7A notice with enclosures is served on proper person
and acknowledgment is kept on record. The service of notice must also be
mentioned in the 7A order.

Web circulation

c) The principals of natural justice must be adhered to during the course of 7A
proceeding and the employer must be allowed reasonable opportunity to
represent their case.

d) While determining dues under Section 7A, the basis of calculation of dues
must be spelt out in the speaking order passed under Section7A.

e). Assessing Authority/Officer must pass speaking order so _ that the orders
do not suffer from any procedural infirmity. Speaking Order includes
discussion of evidence of both the parties and reason for arriving at the
finding.

(This issues with the approval of Central PF Commissioner)

Sub: NATRSS Training Calendar 2016-2017 —reg.
Sir,

The training calendar of NATRSS is being prepared for the financial year 2016-17 (1%
April, 2016 to 31% March, 2017). Approximately 30 training programmes are proposed to be
conducted other than DoP&T sponsored training programmes in which approx 900 officers
have to be nominated for trainings with the idea that each officer undergoes atleast one
training in the year.

The training programmes of the Academy for officers have been broadly categorized
under the following heads:

A. Functional Programmes:-
The programmes related to various aspects of EPF & MP Act 1952, Social Security,
Employees’ Provident Fund Scheme 1952, Employees Pension Scheme 1995, EDLI
Scheme 1976, Establishment and Administration, Right to Information Act, Vigilance
related issues, preparation of Reservation and Rosters, Rajbhasha, Recovery
Management, Natural Justice & Quasi Judicial Proceedings, Compliance & Exemption
and Refresher Course for APFCs.

B. Management Development Programmes
Programmes like Enhancing Managerial Effectiveness, Training of Trainers, Coping
with Retirement, Ethics & value in Public Governance, Communication & Presentation
Skill, Lifestyle Management, Gender Sensitization.

Cc. Faculty Development Programmes
Programmes sponsored by Department of Personnel & Training (DoP&T)

The Group ‘A’ officers are requested to send their preferences for training related to
. their area of interest for atleast three programmes before 19.02.2016 through e-mail at
natrss@epfindia.gov.in so that their preference be kept in view while preparing the
training calendar for the financial year 2016-17.

Subject: Filing of Writ/Appeal/Review within limitation period
Sir

While reviewing the cases lost on technical grounds, it has been observed
that many petitions are dismissed simply because they were filed after lapse of
statutory time limit prescribed under Indian Limitations Act, 1962 or under the
relevant High Court Rules or the Supreme Court Rules, 2013. In case of a review
petition, the time limit prescribed is 30 days from the date of receipt of certified
copy of the judgment.
Be Further, in case of a Writ Petition preferred from the judgment of the
Appellate Tribunal before a High Court, though no statutory time limit is prescribed,
to improve admissibility, it is strongly recommended that such a petition should be
filed as soon as possible, efforts should be made to file within a period of 60 days
from the date of passing of judgment. ;
3. Since every instance of loss in litigation involves long-term adverse
ramification, it is, therefore, exhorted that the instructions contained in the instant
circular should be attached adequate importance.

Yours faithfully

Subject: Submission of Annual Immovable Property Return for the year 2015 (ending

Dear Madam/Sir,

In accordance with the instructions contained in MHA, O.M. No. 25/10/55-Estt. (A)
dated 12" January 1956, every government servant holding a Group ‘A’ or Group ‘B’ post is
required to submit the immovable property return in prescribed format in respect of every
calendar year by 31% January of the next year. Further as per Rule 18(1) (ii) of CCS(Conduct)
Rules, 1964, applicable to EPFO, it is mandatory for all Group ‘A’ and Group ‘B’ officers to
submit their Annual Immovable Property Return.

2. The Annual Immovable Property Return (AIPR) for the year 2015 has become due on
01.01.2016. It is requested to advice all Group ‘A’ & Group 'B’ officers to submit their AIPR
for the year 2015 (as on 01.01.2016) complete in all respect (including full name and signature
with date) within the stipulated time i.e. latest by 31% January 2016 invariably in the prescribed
format annexed herewith.

3. It may be ensured that phrases such as “Same as previous year’, “No change’ etc. are
not used in the AIPR and full particulars of the Immovabie Property inherited/owned/acquired
or held are furnished in all the columns specified in the AIPR in terms of Rule 18 of
CCS(Conduct) Rules, 1964.

4. As per DoPT’s O.M. No. 11012/112007-Estt.A dated 27.09.2011 and MoL&E Circular
No. C-29020/12011-Vig. Dated 02.01.2012 (copy enclosed), vigilance clearance shall be

denied to the officers who do not submit their Annual Immovable Property Return by the
prescribed time limit.

5. Further, appropriate entry regarding late submission/non-submission of AIPRs should
be made in the relevant APARs of the concerned officers in terms of DoPT’s O.M. dated
11.07.2011 and No.2101128/93-Estt.(A) dated 20.10.93.

Sir

Please refer to your E-mail dated 15.01.2016 suggesting that the duration of the

than sufficient for holding “Nidhi Apke Nikat”.

It is clarified that "Nidhi Apke Nikat” was conducted with an endeavour on the part of
the organisation to be more accessible to its different stake holders including employers and
the programme would serve to bring all of them on common platform and facilitate
exchange of ideas and dissemination of information besides of course grievance redressal.

approach as seen in “Bhavishya Nidhi Adalat to a more broad based participatory approach
in “Nidhi Apke Nikat”. It would be in the nature of a publicity outreach programme the
objective of which shall be not only to redress the grievances of the subscribers but also to
invite their suggestions, enable employers to vent their grievances, if any and to sensitise
the stake holders at large about multitude of new initiatives taken in their interest by the

organisation.

Subject: Promotion of Start-Up Ecosystem in India -Instructions regarding inspection
of Start-ups.

Sir/Madam,

Kindly refer to the Secretary (Labour & Employment) D.O Letter No. Z-13025/3 9/2015-LR Cell dated
12.01.2016 regarding promotion of Start-Up Ecosystem in India (Copy enclosed).

In terms of directions contained therein, for the purpose of EPF & MP Act, 1952, all concerned are required
to adhere to the following directions:

a. For the first year of setting up of the Start-ups, such establishments may not be inspected under
EPF & MP Act, 1952. These Start-ups may be asked to submit an online self-declaration instead.

b. Start-Ups are allowed to submit self-certified returns under EPF & MP Act, 1952. From the
second year onwards, up to three year from the setting up of the unit, such Start-Ups may be taken
up for inspection only when very credible and verifiable complaints of violation is filed in writing
and the approval has been obtained Srom the Central Analysis and Intelligence Unit (CAIU).

It is therefore advised to regulate the inspections in the Start-ups, as suggested above, wherever
applicable. For submitting self-certification online, the Shram Suvidha Portal of Government of India
may be used. Pleaase acknowledge the receipt.

(This issues with the approval of the competent authority)

Yours Singerely

Dear ** -

Government of India has decided to promote the Start-Up ecosystem in the country
to incentivize the entrepreneurs in setting up new start-up ventures and thus Catalyze the
creation of employment opportunities through them. In this connection, various incentives
and ease in regulatory compliance provisions are being conceptualized. Start-ups are
defined by Department of Industrial Policy & Promotion (DIPP), as an entity, incorporated or
registered in India not prior to five years, with annual turnover not exceeding Rs. 25 crores
in any preceding financial year, working towards innovation, development, deployment or
commercialization of new products, processes or services driven by technology or
intellectual property.

2: Promoting the Start-ups, as defined above, would need special handholding and
nurturing. Thus such Start-ups, as defined by DIPP, may be allowed to self-certify
compliance with the Labour Laws. The Labour Laws to be covered under this are:

(1) The Industrial Disputes Act, 1947

(2) The Trade Unions Act, 1926

(3) | The Building and Other Constructions Workers’ (Regulation of Employment
and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996 :

(4) — The Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946

(5) The Inter-State Migrant Workmen (Regulation of Employment and Conditions
of Service) Act, 1979

(6) The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972

(7) The Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970

_ {8) The Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
(9) | The Employees’ State Insurance Act, 1948

3. It is observed that out of the 9 Central Labour Acts above, first 7 Acts are
implemented both by State Government (State Sphere) and Central Government (Central
sphere). Last two (EPF and ESI! Act) are mainly implemented by Central Government. Also.
out of these 9, only 6 Acts (viz. Industrial Disputes Act, Building & Other Construction
Workers Act, Inter-State Migrant Workmen Act, Contract Labour Act, EPF Act and ESI! Act)
require establishments to file Return. Similarly, only 6 Acts (viz Building & Other
Construction Workers Act, Inter-State Migrant Workmen Act, Payment of Gratuity Act,
Contract Labour Act, EPF Act and ES! Act) require inspection of the establishments by
Inspectors.

4, In view of the above, for implementation of the above 9 Acts in the Central sphere. it

SUBJECT: Consolidated Guidelines regarding securing Compliance in respect of EPF members
proceeding to work in a foreign country

Sir

References have been received in Central Office regarding the compliance status of
Indian employees working in a covered establishment and moving to work in a foreign country. It
has been observed that different offices are adopting varied practices with regard to continuance
of compliance of such employees while they are working or proceeding to work in a foreign
country. Thus, need has been feit to revisit the same and bring a consolidated set of guidelines to
handle possible scenarios..

The fundamental principle of deduction and depositing of PF and other dues is
based on the assumption that wages are either paid or are payable by the establishment. Thus
contributions are deducted and deposited with Employees’ Provident Fund Organization if wages
are paid or payable by the Indian establishment. However if wages are neither paid nor payable
out of the books of the Indian establishment, then PF and other contributions are not to be
deducted.

sine qua non for implementation of the policy guidelines. In order to facilitate the officers to exercise
options vis-a-vis the vacancies available at different stations/offices and tenure (three years at a station

Subject : Timely action in all Contempt Cases arising out of staff matters - regarding.
Sir,

Instructions have been issued from time to time from Legal Cell and HRM Division on handling of cases at
various legal fora in connection with EPF Staff Service matters and procedure for filing the counter reply on behalf of
Union of India and on behalf of Central Provident Fund Commissioner, wherever they are impleaded as respondents.
Similarly, extant instructions have been issued to take prompt action in contempt cases. An exhaustive circular was
issued by Head Office from Legal Cell on 27.05.2014 in this regard which is self explanatory.

2. It is observed that even in contempt cases arising out of not carrying out the orders passed by various High
Courts and Benches of Central Administrative Tribunals are not properly followed up in time which leads to contempt
and causes embarrassment at the eleventh hour.

3. While reviewing the contempt cases, CPFC has expressed his displeasure on the callous approach exhibited by
RPFCs posted in field offices in dealing with legal cases.

4. All the RPFCs In-Charge of Regional/Sub Regional Offices, while carrying out the instructions as contained in
the Head Office circulars, dated 09.12.2013 (placed in the official website at SI. No.578 in 2013-14 of Circular and
Orders segment), 27.05.2014 (placed in the official website at SI. No.155 in 2014-15 of Circular and Orders
segment), 08.07.2014 (placed in the official website at Sl. No.258 in 2014-15 of Circular and Orders segment) and
12.11.2014 (placed in the official website at SI. No.580 in 2014-15 of Circular and Orders segment) ensure that
appropriate and timely action are taken to avoid the contempt.

5. It has also been decided that as regards the cases filed at various benches of Central Administrative Tribunal,
the Regional PF Commissioner posted in the offices at the places where Central Administrative Tribunals are located
should monitor such cases and maintain liaison with other field offices and Head Office and to take prompt action
and to avoid contempt.

6. Any deviation noticed will be viewed seriously.

Yours faithfully, -

Subject : Annual General Transfer 2016 - Calling for option — regarding.
Sir,

The Transfer Policy in the cadre of Commissioners has already been circulated vide Head Office
Letter No. HRD/3/2015/Pr.II/34825 dated 06.01.2016 (placed in the official website at SI. No. 596 of the
‘Circular and Office Order Segment’) for information of all concerned and thus available in the public
domain. In accordance with the guidelines incorporated in the said Transfer Policy, the Annual General
Transfer of Group ‘A’ officers is required to be made during the year, 2016 alongwith consequential
administrative arrangements.

2. The Transfer Policy envisages that correct database of officers reflecting their posting profile is a
sine qua non for implementation of the policy guidelines. In order to facilitate the officers to exercise
options vis-a-vis the vacancies available at different stations/offices and tenure (three years at a station
or nine years in the Zone) completed by the officers, the relevant information relating to Group ‘A’
officers, are hereby placed in the official website. The individual officers and the controlling officers
(Regional Provident Fund Commissioners, In-Charge of the Region) can access to the data from the
following links hereby provided in the official website. The links provided are as under:

(i) | RPFC (Grade I) — Disposition/vacancy — link RPFC_I_Vacancy

(ii) | RPFC (Grade I) — Posting Profile — link RPFC_I_PP

(iii) |. RPFC (Grade II)- summary of present vacancy — link RPFC_II_Vacancy
(iv) RPFC (Grade II) — Posting Profile — link RPFC_II_PP

(v) | RPFC (Grade II) — Disposition/vacancy — link RPFC_II_Disposition

(vi) APFC - Officewise summary of present vacancy — link APFC_Vacancy
(vii) APFC-— Disposition/vacancy — link APFC_Disposition

(viii) Option format — link Option.Xls ZO / RO NATRSS/ZTI

3; As the data is required to be properly routed through and consolidated at Regional Offices, the
following instructions need to be complica with.

(i) All options in respect of officers posted at Sub-Regional Offices be obtained, consolidated
and forwarded by Regional Office to Head Office in the designated e-mail ID. Similarly,
Additional CPFC-II (ASD) will obtain the options from all the officers posted at Head Office,
compile and forward the same to Head Office in the dedicated e-mail ID.

(ii) The Zonal Offices will consolidate the data in respect of their offices and send to the
controlling Regional Office for onward transmission to Head Office. The officers In-Charge
of Zonal Training Institutes will obtain the option in respect of officers working under them
and consolidate and forward the same to Director NATRSS who in turn will forward the
complete data in respect of all ZTIs to Head Office in the designated e-mail ID.

Training Institutes/Sub-Zonal Training Institutes.

(iv) The data in excel sheet shall be sent to Head Office in the dedicated e-mail ID by the

Sub: Payment of contribution by the employers by 15" of the following month —
Removing of grace period of 5 days.

Sir/Madam,

As per paragraph 38(1) of the EPF Scheme, 1952, paragraph 3 of EPS, 1995 and paragraph
8(1) of EDLI Scheme, 1976, the employers are required to pay the contributions and
administrative charges within fifteen days of close of every month. The employer, as per para
5.1.3 of Manual of Accounting Procedure (Part-I General), is also allowed a grace period of 5
days to remit the contribution.

2. The grace period of five days have been allowed for the employers to remit the
contributions as the system of calculation of wages of the employees and their corresponding
dues under the three schemes (Employees’ Provident Fund Scheme 1952, Employees’ Pension
Scheme 1995 & Employees’ Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme 1976) were done manually and its
remittances in the bank required additional time in the earlier manual setup.

3 In the present era, employers compute the wages and EPF liabilities electronically (in
most of the cases on real time basis) and file Electronic Challan-cum-Return (ECR). The
remittances are also being deposited through Internet Banking. This has reduced the process and
time taken in calculation of PF dues and its remittances in the bank. Accordingly, it has been
decided that concession of grace period of 5 days available to the employers for depositing the
contribution & other dues is withdrawn herewith. This decision shall apply from February, 2016
(contributions for month of January, 2016 and payable in the month of February, 2016).

4. The employers shall pay the contribution and other dues as envisaged under EPF & MP
Act, 1952 and Schemes framed thereunder within fifteen days of close of every month

5. This has approval of Central P.F. Commissioner.

petitioner is able to justify how such disclosure would be in public interest

3. Hon’ble CIC thus disposed the second filed by the applicant Shri Sachin Arya

Subject: Incorporating of the State Emblem of India - regarding.

Dear Madan/Sir,

Instances came to the notice of Head Office that the officers of the organization are using the State
Emblem of India in their correspondences and in their visiting cards. So much so, the State Emblem of India
was utilized while issuing the identity cards to the officers and staff of the organization. A reference was made
to the Ministry of Labour & Employment for incorporating the State Emblem of India in the official logo of
EPFO. The Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India, while informing the disagreement of
Ministry of Home Affairs for incorporation of the State Emblem of India in the official logo adopted by
autonomous bodies, directed EPFO to adopt a logo without incorporating the State Emblem of India in it.

2. Subsequently, Ministry of Home Affairs vide their notification dated 04.10.2007 specified the list of
Authorities/Ministries or Departments of the Central / State Governments who are authorized to use the State
Emblem of India. It was felt that the authorities specified in the Employees’ Provident Funds & Miscellaneous
Provisions Act, 1952 (the Act), an Act of Parliament, are the authorities competent to use the State Emblem of
India in their correspondences while implementing the Act. Accordingly, a reference was further made to
Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India to take up the issue of using State Embiem of India _ in
official correspondences etc. with the Ministry of Home Affairs as per the Schedules of State Emblem of India
(Regulation of use) Rules, 2007.

3. Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India referred the matter to the Ministry of Home
Affairs from time to time and last such reference was made on 29.05.2015. In reply to that and after
examination, Ministry of Home Affairs did not agree to the proposal regarding the use of State Embtem of India
in the Official Logo of EPFO as the EPFO does not come under the category of ‘Commission’ or ‘Authority’
established or constituted by an Act of Parliament or set up by the Central Government. The same has been
communicated to Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India. A copy of the same is attached
herewith.

4. Ail concerned are thus advised to ensure that the State Emblem of India is not used in various
correspondences, visiting cards, identity cards etc. in EPFO.

Yours faithfully

Addl. Central P.F. Commissioner(HQRS.)

Subject : Transfer Policy of Group ‘A’ officers of EPFO - regarding.

Sir/Madam,

Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in its judgment dated 31.10.2013 in the Writ Petition (Civil)
No.82 of 2011 in the case of T.S.R. Subramanian & Ors. Vs. Union of India & Ors. passed orders for
maintaining transparency in the matters of transfer and postings of officers and to ensure a fixed tenure
of posting. It had also directed to constitute Civil Services Board (CSB) to ensure fairness in these
matters. Pursuant to the judgement, the Department of Personnel & Training, Government of India,
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions issued instructions in their Office Memorandums -
(i) No. 11013/10/2013-Estt.A dated 26.12.2013 and (ii) No. 11013/10/2013-Estt.A dated 09.01.2014 for
implementation of the judgment dated 31.10.2013 of Hon'ble Supreme Court.

2. It was stipulated by Department of Personnel & Training in their instructions that there should be
a committee depending on the hierarchy of the service of the organisation to consider the posting and
transfer of officers. The Committee would be a recommendatory body and final decision would rest with
the Competent Authority as per the rules. There should be a minimum tenure prescribed for different
posts. The transfer of any officer before completion of the minimum tenure may be done in public
interest but the reasons of the same should be recorded. The composition of the Committee and the
transfer policy should be formally notified and they may also be placed in the public domain.

3. The Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India, while forwarding such instructions
issued by Department of Personne! and Training, Government of India, Ministry of Personnel, Public
Grievances & Pensions, directed EPFO to frame a transfer policy on the lines of the instructions.
Accordingly, in consonance to the judgement of the Hon'bie Supreme Court and the instructions issued
by formulated a Transfer Policy for regulating the transfer of Group 'A' Officers and the same has
already been approved by the Competent Authority.

4, The approved Transfer Policy is hereby placed on public domain and thus notified for
information of all the officers.

“5, The Ministry of Labour & Employment vide their letter No. A-11017/03/2014-SS-I dated
23.07.2015 conveyed the decision of the Hon'ble Chairman, Central Board of Trustees/ Union Minister
of State (Independent Charge) for Labour & Employment on constitution of the " EPF Officers’ Transfer
Committee (EOTC) " and on the powers of the Competenet Authority for transfer. The details are as
under:

a) The ‘Transfer Committee ‘ shall consist of the following:

i. Joint Secretary (SS), Ministry of Labour & Employment

ii, Director (SS)/Deputy Secretary (SS), Ministry of Labour & Employment
ii. Additional CPFC (HQRS), EPFO
iv. Additional -CPFC/I/i, Head Quarters/NATRSS

b) Central Provident Fund Commissioner will be Competent Authority for approval for all levels.
However all cases of premature transfers , deviations from norms, compassionate ground,
appeals etc. would be put to Minister/Chairman, CBT.

Subject:- Ensuring compliance in respect of multi-location establishments
Sir,

Enrolment of workers engaged by multi-location establishments, especially through
contractors or on contract is an enduring issue. Most of the complaints relating to nonenrolment of employees under EPFO is found pertaining to this category of employees.
Parliamentary committees have been seized of the matter and instructions have been
received from Government of India also to ensure that all such employees are enrolled
under EPFO and extended due benefits.

2. The matter has been reviewed and following instructions are being issued to ensure
enrolment of all such eligible employees under EPFO:-

i. It shall be the responsibility of the concerned RO/SRO to ensure that. all
employees working within its physical jurisdiction and who are eligible to be
enrolled as PF members are so enrolled.

ii. This has to be ensured irrespective of the fact whether any of such employees
belong to an establishment which has been issued the PF code number by
another RO/SRO.

iii. The RO/SRO within whose jurisdiction such employees are working shall be
referred to as "Local office” for the purpose of ensuring compliance of such
employees under the EPF and MP Act, 1952. The RO/SRO where the
establishment is registered under the EPF and MP Act, 1952, even though its
employees are working into the physical jurisdiction of another RO/SRO, shall be
referred as "Main office” for the purpose of ensuring compliance in respect of
such employees under the Act.

iv. The Local office shall cause inspection of the establishment, record the
particulars of the employees found working on-site and verify the compliance
status in respect of all such employees. The verification in respect of employees

belonging to establishments registered with Local office shall be done with
reference to office records.

For verifying compliance status of employees belonging to an establishment
which has been issued EPF code number by another RO/SRO, the Local office
shall ensure that a reference is made to the said Main office containing details
of the on-site physical inspection visit.

The said reference shall include name, father’s/spouse’s name, date of birth, date
of joining, wages, UAN/PF account number (if available), PAN (if available),
Aadhaar (if available) and mobile number (if available).

The Main office, once it receives a reference from the local office, shall verify its
records and if required cause physical inspection of the registered office of the
establishment within its jurisdiction and submit a comprehensive report to the
Local office containing the details specifically in respect of the employees
whose list has been received from the local office as also any other details which
are revealed by such inspection.

The Main office shall complete this task in not more than 30 days after
receiving a reference from the Local office.

Thus, irrespective of the RO/SRO where the PF code number has been issued to an

establishment, it shall be the responsibility of the RO/SRO within whose jurisdiction
employees of such establishments are physically working, to ensure compliance under the
EPF and MP Act, 1952.

Subject: Accounting Policy and method of accounting for equity and related
investment

As you may be aware that a New Pattern of Investment has been notified by
Ministry of Labour & Employment both for EPFO and Exempted Provident Funds
vide notification dated 23.04.2015 and 29.05.2015 separately. As per the New
Pattern of Investment the Trusts have to invest minimum of 5% of the total
investment in equity and related investments. Since equity as an asset class is
different from fixed income securities their treatment for accounting purpose was a
cause of concern among many of the exempt Provident Fund.

2. In order to arrive at a most Prudent accounting policy and method of
accounting for equity and related investment a draft accounting policy and method
of accounting for equity and related investment was also circulated for comments
from various stakeholders. Based on the suggestions received a draft policy on the

Accounting policy and method of Accounting for equity & related Investment

1.
The Central Board of Trustees (CBT), EPF in its 207th Meeting decided to
investment 05% of its corpus in Exchange Traded Fund (ETF) under the
category (iv) i.e. Equities and related investments of pattern of Investment
notified by Ministry of Labour & Employment vide notification no. 1071 (E) dated
23rd April, 2015. This is the first time, EPFO has decided to invest in equity and
related instruments in financial year 2015-16.

2.
To provide method of accounting and accounting policy for equity and related
investments, EPFO would require to frame accounting policy for equity and
related investment. So far the investment in EPFO is only in such fixed income
securities which pays interest either quarterly, half year or yearly. The assets
have been held till maturity. The interest received has been treated as profit as
per the cash system of accounting being followed by EPFO. Profit so calculated
has been distributed among the beneficiary as per the provisions of para 60 of
Employees’ Provident Fund Scheme. Since the fixed income assets have been
valued at cost of acquisition in the closing stock, capital gain or loss due to
change in valuation have not been accounted for in these assets.

3.
As against the above characteristics of fixed income assets where the income is
actually derived from interest, which is revenue in nature, the profit in the equity
will mostly be capital in nature and will be represented by its current market
value as compared to its cost of acquisition. However, the dividend received on
underlying shares of ETF, will be revenue in nature having characteristic similar
to interest income.

4.
Secondly, EPFO being a Pension Fund is likely to have long term investment in
equity. It will not be prudent to sale the asset at the end of the year in order to
realise profit in cash for its distribution among the beneficiaries. This will
unnecessarily introduce the concept of repeated transaction cost during the
sale for booking the profit and purchase in subsequent month from the fresh
receipts.

Subject: Arrangement for using services of officers/ officials posted in the Official
Language Wing on tour basis for operative efficiency - regarding.

Dear Madam/Sir,

References have been received from various field offices from time to time regarding
shortage of officers and staff in the Official Language Wing. Similar requests have also been
received from field offices when Parliamentary Committee on Official Language propose to visit
the offices that have vacancies in the cadre of Official Lanquage.

2. A redistribution of responsibilities amongst the existing officers and staff in this wing is
the suggested mechanism. The officers and officials working in this wing under the control of
Addl. CPFC (Zones) need to be utilized for discharging additional responsibilities on tour basis
in offices where their services are warranted. It is in this background and in order to meet the
requirements of various offices in this area, it has been decided to authorize Addl. CPFC
(Zones) to utilize the existing manpower available in this cadre under their jurisdiction in such
a way that the work related to Official Language in none of the offices gOe# unattended.

3. In cases of detailing the officers/staff on tour basis, the tour programme shall be
approved by the Addl. CPFC (Zones) in exercise of the revised powers delegated to them under
Sl. No. 10 of the “Delegation of Powers to Addl. CPFCs (Zones) and Addl. CPFC (HR) under the
Head - “Allowing tour to officers and staff” (Original Item No. 95). Further, the tour programme
of the concerned officers/officials need to be proposed by the senior most officer of the Official
Language Wing working under the administrative control of the Addl. CPEC (Zones) on need
basis. Such delegated powers should be sparingly used by the Addl. CPFC (Zones) at the time
of need and not as a routine.

4, Accordingly, all the Addi. CPFC (Zones) are requested to work out a mechanism for
optimum use of the existing officers and officials in the Official Language Wing so that the work
related to Official Language does not suffer in any of the offices under their jurisdiction under
intimation to Head Office.

REVIEW MEETING FOR UAN ACTIVATION
(NATRSS, New Delhi; 19th December 2015)


The list of officers who attended the meeting is attached as annexure.
1.
ACC(HQ) RB initiated the meeting by informing the participants about the rationale
behind issuing the circular dated 17-12-205 making UAN mandatory with effect from 01-01-2016.
He stated that the instructions have been issued to ensure that UAN is made fully functional and
the members can avail of the benefits, post retirement, on the basis of combined service across
various employments. He advised the field officers to ensure that all possible help is extended to
establishments in getting KYC details of members to whom UAN has been issued as well as in
completing the member profile. This, is also important for smooth start of the next phase of
computerisation reform in the EPFO wherein most of the services will be available to members
and establishments online.
2.
The Central PF Commissioner advised all the officers present that they have been chosen
as pilot offices for completion of members profile as well as KYC seeding of all the members to
whom UAN has been issued. He informed that the learnings from the exercise carried out by this
group of offices will be replicated across India to make UAN a success in complete sense of the
word. He advised the officers present to state the challenges envisaged by them in completing
the task as well as the resources required for effective and timely completion of the same. He
also informed that it has been seen that more than 80% of UAN belonged to about 10% of the
establishments and focusing on these 10% of establishments will ensure that bulk of the task is
completed in a time bound manner. Establishments may be contacted and advised either to
provide date of exit against the UAN issued to employees in the establishment; failing which
member particulars, namely date of birth, date of joining, father’s/spouse’s name and KYC
details, primarily Aadhaar and bank account number with IFSC code of the bank branches be
seeded in the member master. The objective is to capture Form 11(New) details and not just
activation of UAN. Activation of UAN without getting details of members is hindering providing
of services.
3.
The Central PF Commissioner stated that EPFO has launched UAN based claims
settlement wherein attestation of claim forms by employers has been done away with. He stated
that we should aim at having at least one third of claims through UAN based claim forms and for
this purpose updation of members master is essential along with getting KYC details, particularly
seeding of Aadhaar in member master should be impressed upon the establishments as well as
the member, more so when the Hon’ble Supreme Court has said that Aadhaar can be used for
providing provident fund benefits. He advised IS division to explore the possibility of Aadhaar
based information verification of members so that their claims can be settled expeditiously.
4.
The Central PF Commissioner advised the headquarters team to develop the matrix for
grading employers on the basis of their employment size, contribution and compliance record.

Sir,

The Secretary General, All India EPF Staff Federation vide their letter dated
17.09.2015 addressed to Hon'ble Chairman, Central Board of Trustees, EPF, Secretary,
Labour & Employment, Government of India and the Central Provident Fund
Commissioner wherein the intent of the AIEPFSF to go for agitation on account of non
redressal of long pending staff issues.

2. In this regard, it is to inform that the Additional CPFC (HQRS) took a meeting
with the office bearers of AIEPFSF where all the pending issues with regard to staff
were discussed. The issues like sanction of additional posts , grant of relaxation with
regard to eligible service for promotion to the next higher grade, pay anomalies,
amendment to the Recruitment Rules which are too old, stagnation in certain
cadres etc. could not be resolved where approval of the Central Board of Trustees,
EPF and the Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India is required.

pending demand for cadre restructuring in the organization. It was decided that the
feeling of the Federation will be escalated to the Hon'ble Chairman, Central Board of
Trustees for appropriate decision.

has convened a special meeting on 09.12.2015 only to discuss the issue of
Organizational Restructuring. It was also informed that the Central Board has
constituted a Sub-Committee under the Chairmanship of Additional Secretary to
Government of India, Ministry of Labour & Employment to redress the grievances of
staff and officers with regard to the Organizational Restructuring. As per the
decision, reference has been made to Hon'ble Chairman, Central Board of Trustees
through Vice Chairman for issue of orders on constitution of the Sub-Committee so
that in-depth study could be made by the Sub-Committee. It is expected that the
AIEPFSF should honour and respect the decision of the Board.

Subject: Rate of interest to be charged by RO/SRO from link branches of SBI
for non-transferring the credit balance lying in A/c No. 1, 2, 10 & 21 to
respective central accounts- reg.

Sir,
With the commencement of electronic transmission facility, remittance by

employers of statutory dues using net banking platform is gaining popularity. This
facility permits that dues can be transmitted at any hour of the day including those after
the close of working hours of bank branch. Bank sweep transfers the remittances received
during working hours of a day but, as reported, not those received after the close of its
working hours. In this regard, references have been received from field offices seeking
clarification as to whether the interest is to be levied and collected on such balance that
remains with link branch for that day without being transferred to the Mumbai Main

Branch (MMB), SBI.

2: In this connection, the relevant provisions are contained in clause (9) read
with clause (8) of Para 5.19.2 of the “AGREEMENT REGARDING BANKING
ARRANGEMENT OF FUNDS BELONGING TO AN UNDER. THE CONTROL OF

Subject: Succession Certificates being called for by field offices in

Sir,

It has been brought to the notice of headquarters that certain field offices
are insisting on a succession certificates from a Court of Law from the dependants/
beneficiaries under EPS, 95 in settlement of pension cases especially in death cases
resulting in hardship to beneficiaries to get their claims settled.

ve In this connection, it is informed that Manual of Accounting Procedure
(MAP) in Part II A Chapter 10 and MAP Part III (EPS) Chapter 7 deals with payment to
nominees and procedures to be adopted in the absence of nomination. Generally,
succession certificates are called from claimants only where there is doubt about title of
claimant or rival claimants.

3: All RPFCs, Incharge of Regional Offices/Officers-Incharge, Sub Regional
Offices are requested to ensure that Provisions of MAP should be followed by the offices
under their jurisdiction in dealing with pension cases, particularly death cases where
there is no valid nomination in existence. Also, as all the field offices have clear
provisions to deal with nominations and family members claimants in the normal course
succession certificates should not be insisted upon. Only in cases where there are
disputes or doubts, a succession certificate may be called for.

4. Further, it may also be ensured that in those instances where succession
certificate is felt necessary such certificate should be accepted from authorities who are
authorized under law to issue such certificates. In the event of doubt as to which
authority is authorized under the prevalent law for issuing such certifi cates, legal opinion
‘should be taken and any orders issued by the State Governments in such matters should
be obtained and decision taken accordingly.

ORDER
Subject: Digital signature is mandatory for online registrationregarding.
In view of the direction issued by the Government of India (the Ministry of
Labour & Employment) under para 78 of the EPF Scheme, t952,
I, K.K.Jalan, Central Provident Fund Commissioner, hereby issue the following
directives:
(a) The employer of the establishment coverable under the Act and
applying for Provident Fund Code online shall submit application along
with all prescribed documents online after digitally signing the same.
Therefore, it is necessary for every establishment to have a digital
signature.
(b) The employers of all the establishments already covered under the Act,
must have digital signature so that they can submit any document in
future such as form 5A digitally also. It will also enable the
establishment to verify UAN data.
2.
These directives are made operative with immediate effect. The
present establishments already covered (having employees less than 50),
however, are given time till 3L.L2.2015 for procuring and registering the
digital signature.
