In Exercise of powers conferred under para 78 of Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme

“a. The employees whose details like AADHAR Number and Bank Account Number

claims in Form-19, Form-10C and Form 31 directly to the Commissioner without
attestation of their employers, in such form and manner as may be specified by

b. The above direction be made operational with immediate effect.”

Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme 1952, Central Provident Fund Commissioner, hereby
prescribe the new forms 19 UAN, 10C UAN and 31 UAN for all employees whose AADHAR
Number and Bank details have been seeded as KYC and have been duly verified by the

employer using digital signature and the details in form No. 11 new have been completed.

claims of withdrawal in existing form No. 19, 10C & 31, as the case may be.

4. It is reiterated that form No. 19 UAN, form No. 10C UAN and form No. 31 UAN need
not be attested by employer and should be submitted by the employee directly to the

respective jurisdictional EPF Office.

Sir/ Madam,
As the HR Software launched for EPFO employees is presently handling
the details of the currently employed employees, it has been decided by the
Competent Authority to provide a facility for the Pensioners also and handling of
the post retirement functions for them. A note in this regard has been received
from the ACC (HQ) HRM.
2.
To facilitate this, there is a need to issue the EID for our retired
employees also. The revised format for the generation of the EID for the retired
employees is attached and is also available in the login of the Users under the
Help Link.
3.
All Regional Offices/Head Office/NATRSS/ZTIs are requested to kindly
prepare a list of pensioners drawing pension from their respective office. The
entire list with the following details should be mailed to the RPFC, NDC in the
following format:
Sl. No., Name of the Employee, Designation at the time or retirement/death,
date of death (if applicable only) {in xls only}
4.
EID generation request should be sent in the revised format to the RPFC,
NDC for such employees who do not have the EID generated. The search facility
in the HR Software facilitates checking whether an employee has got EID or not.
As in other cases the EID generation request for the EPF Pensioners/Deceased
Employees where Pension is being disbursed to family, may be sent to the
following e-mail id:
hr. so ftwareaepfindia. gov . in
5.
In case of the employees who have since deceased and the family is
drawing pension also the EID will be generated in the name of employee only
and the Pension Function will link them to the beneficiaries.

Yours faitylfully---.
nganath)

6.

the pensioner are not required and the EID request may be certified by the
APFC looking after the Pension cases.

Subject: Mandatory publication of Tender Enquiries on the Central Public
Procurement Portal

Pursuant to the decisions of the Group of Ministers constituted to consider
measures to tackle corruption and improve transparency, on the
recommendations of the Committee on Public Procurement set up to look into
various issues having an impact on public procurement policy, standards and
procedures, it has been decided that:

a. NIC will set up a portal called the Central Public Procurement
Portal (hereinafter referred to as CPP Portal) with an e-publishing
module (similar to NIC's website www.tenders.gowin ) and an eprocurement module (similar to NIC’s e-procurement sites such as
pmgsytenders gov.in and epro-nicsi.nic.in ). The CPP Portal will be
accessible at the URL eprocure.gov.in and will provide links to the
non-NIC e-procurement sites being used at present by various
Ministries/ Departments, CPSEs and autonomous/ statutory
bodies.

b. While e-publishing of tender enquiries. corrigenda thereto and
details of contracts awarded thereon, on the Portal, shall be made
mandatory in a phased manner wef 1° January 2012, the
comprehensive end-to-end e -Procurement feature would be
implemented in a phased manner w.ef. 1* April 2012, for which
instructions will be issued separately. in the meantime, Digital
Signature, which. is essential at the e-procurement phase, may be
obtained from any Certifying Authority or from NIC which is also a

, Certifying Authority, for the concerned officials.

E-Publishing:

c. It will be mandatory for all Ministries/ Departments of the
Central Government, their attached and subordinate Offices,
Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) and autonomous/
statutory bodies to publish their tender enquiries, corrigenda
thereon and details of bid awards on the CPP Portal using epublishing module with effect from the following dates:

c.i, Ministries/ Departments and their attached and
subordinate offices w.e.f. 1°' January 2012:

c.ii. CPSEs w.e.f. 1°' February 2012;
¢.iii. Autonomous/statutory bodies w.e.f. 1° April, 2012.

Subject: Trainers Development Programme — Experiential Learning Tools (EL1)- 14. 12.2015 to
18.12.2015-Sponsored by DoP&T- Inviting Nominations- Regarding.
Sir,

National Academy for Training & Research in Social Security (NATRSS), New Delhi, a unit of
Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation under the Ministry of Labour, Govt. of India is organizing a National
level training course on Training of Trainers (ToT) namely Experiential Learning Tools (ELT)- 14" to 18"
December 2015 to be conducted under Trainers Development Programmes prepared and sponsored by
Department of Personnel & Training (DoP&T) Govt. of India during the calendar year 2015-2016.

ELT aims at equipping the participants with skills relevant to the learner-centered training-process
through the mode of experiential learning; particularly in the application of identified training
methodologies namely Case Study, Field Visit and Role Play; besides appropriately using Skill Development

Exercises.

The trainers will be certified recognized Master Trainers (MTs)/ Recognized Trainers (RTs) of DoPT,
Govt. of India.

No course fee will be charged as per the instructions of DoP&T. TA/DA in respect of the participant
will also be borne by the sponsoring authority / organization.

The Course is fully residential. National Academy for Training & Research in Social Security has
modest hostel facility.

It is requested to send the nominations of eligible officers from your esteemed Department/
Organisation/ Institution. The nominations dully filled in the specific format (enclosed) should reach
NATRSS at the earliest possible preferably by 30.11.2015 by Fax on O11- 28525987 or e-mail us at:
natrss@epfindia.gov.in to enable us to make proper arrangements for the participants. After scrutiny
of the application, the Department / Organisation / Institution will be informed and the selected
participants will be provided the course material in advance to enhance the learning process.

For any further information about the NATRSS or training programmes, please feel free to contact at
Telephone No.011-28524248. The application for nomination of participants and sponsoring Authority's
confirmation format are enclosed.

The National Academy for Training & Research in Social Security has been conducting
Workshop on International Workers for Establishments under Employees’ Provident Fund
and Miscellaneous Provisions Act 1952 for the last several years.

the developments in EPF & EPS Administration, we have designed a one day Workshop on

international workers under the provisions of the EPF & MP Act,1952.

Coverage of International Workers under EPF&MP Act

Bilateral agreements

FAQs on international workers

morning of the end of the programme i.e.01.12.2015.

Ref: 1.This office Letter No.C-III/4(25)2006/DL/NZ/14591 dated 04 Sep. 2014
2.This office Letter No.C-III/4(25)2006/DL/NZ/15253 dated 25 Nov. 2013

Sir,

Please refer to this office letters cited above on the captioned subject matter.
Vide the letter cited second, the you were requested to generate Penal Damages
Reports upto 31-12-2013 based on functionality provided in the new application
software and levy penal damages under Section 14B and interest under Section 7Q
of the EPF & MP Act 1952. Vide letter cited first you were required to furnish monthly
report on progress achieved in levy of Penal Damages U/S 14B and Interest U/S 7Q
of the Act.

2: It is seen that as per the information available in this office that while some
Offices have promptly initiated action for levy of Penal Damages and Interest for further
period from 1.1.2014 onwards, many offices have not taken this activity on regular
monthly basis as required. In this connection, you may note that interest under Section
7Q is towards making good the loss incurred by the Fund due to belated remittances
while Penal Damages under Section 14B is a deterrent on employers from recurrence
of belated remittances. Prompt remittance of dues by employers ensures timely credit
of accumulations to member’s accounts and facilitates timely settlement of claims.
Any delay in action in this regard by field offices results in further loss to the Fund by
way of interest on investible funds and leads to ineffective client’ service in terms of
resultant loss of distributable interest to members.

3. You are advised to ensure that the application software functionality is put to
effective use and the reports are generated on a monthly basis without fail for big
defaulters involving probable penal damages of more than Rs.1 lakh. In any case levy
of Interest under Section 7Q and Penal Damages under Section 14B of the Act in

respect of any defaulting establishment should not be delayed beyond 6 months. You
are also advised to ensure that no undue adjournments are allowed and cases are
promptly disposed and dues recovered without any delay. Monthly progress achieved
by your office may be furnished to this office in the attached format by email so as to
reach this office on or before 5" of the following month without fail to Additional Central
Provident Fund Commissioner of Zone. Reports for all ROs/SROs will be sent by
ACCs of Zones to Head Office.

4. The Additional Central Provident Fund Commissioner in charge of Zone is
requested to monitor this activity on a regular basis and ensure prompt action by all
offices under their jurisdiction.

Circular 0 9 oct 2015

it is observed that CPIOs in EPF Headquarters are forwarding RTI applications (or part thereof) to
CPIO (Conference) wherein the applicant has requested for agenda and minutes of all the relevant
meetings of CBT/EC wherein a specific issue was discussed and approved by the CBT/EC.

The agenda and minutes of the CBT/EC meetings held till date are available on EPFO website
‘www.epfindia.gov.in’ and are placed in public domain in accordance with Section 4(1) of the RTI Act.
Transmitting specific requests regarding any particular issue discussed by CBT/EC to CPIO (Conference) is
not proper as the concerned CPIO which is holding the information in his capacity as the RPFC
concerned of a particular branch is the custodian of information regarding the specific number and date
of meetings of CBT and EC in which the said issue was discussed.

Routine transfer of such requests to CPIO (Conference) would tantamount to denial of
information by the concerned CPIOs, as_ they, in their capacity as RPFC concerned of any particular
division are holding the information and it should accordingly be disseminate to the applicant. The
Conference Branch of EPF Headquarter is only the custodian of agenda and minutes of the CBT and EC
which are placed in the public domain and available to everybody.

in view of the foregoing, it is advised that the concerned CPIOs in EPF Headquarter and/or RPFC
(PID) should not routinely transfer such RTI requests to Conference Branch unless the subject matter of
RTI request pertains to functioning of the Conference Branch. It is advised that in future RTI requests
may be handled accordingly.

Sir,

for seeking guidance in legal matters/cases without specifically mentioning the
point/issue on which the Head Office guidance is being solicited.

Subject: Special Recovery Drive during the month of September,2015.

Sir,

The performance of Field Offices in the area of recovery of Current
Demand (CD) and Arrear Demand (AD) during Special Recovery Drive for the
month of September,2015 has been reviewed.

Recovery of Current Demand (Un-Exempted):
(i) As per the instructions contained in Head Office circular dated 19.06.2012

(placed in the Official Website of the Organization at Sl. No.187/2012),
the targets set in the area of recovery of Current Demand is 100%. It is
observed that during Special Recovery Drive for the month of September,
2015, all the Regions failed to achieve the fixed target. Only Mangalore
and Ahmedabad Regions have made recovery above 30% whereas rest of

the Regions’ performance of recovery in this area is very low.

Recovery of Current Demand (Exempted):

(ii) In the area of Current Demand (Exempted), it is observed that out of all
40 Regions, only 01 Regional Office i.e. Patna has performed excellent
achieving the target of 100% recovery which is well appreciated. Ludhiana
and Hyderabad Regions have made recovery 42.39% & 38.52%
respectively whereas the performance of rest of the Regions are not very

encouraging.

Contd...

- s
Recovery of Arrear Demand (Un-Exempted & Exempted):

(iii) As per the instructions contained in Head Office circular dated 19.06.2012
(placed in the Official Website of the Organization at Sl. No.187/2012),
the targets set in the area of recovery of Current Demand is 80%. It is
observed that performance of all Regions exccept Mangalore, Chandigarh
and Raipur Regions is not upto the mark which is highly regretted. Low
percentage of recovery in the above area shows ineffectiveness and poor
monitoring in handling Compliance Machinery. All the ACCs of the Zones
are requested to ensure that the target so fixed is achieved in a time
bound manner.

In view of above, all ACCs are, therefore, requested to make a
concrete Action Plan with in a fortnight & convey to Head Office. All out
efforts need to be taken to recover, the Current Demand & Arrear Demand,
also deploy suitable officers/officials so as to check the mounting Arrears
and to reach the target by the year end.

Sir,
A reference was received in which a clarification
on the status of student- trainee vis-a-vis the provision of
the Employee Provident Funds & Miscellaneous
Provisions Act, 1952 was sought from Head Office.
2.
It is a matter
of common
observation
that now-a-days
most technical!professional
educational
institutes
impart industrial
training/
practical
on the job
training
to their students
as an integral
component
of academic
curriculum. During such training period, student-trainees
are exposed to modern technical development
and hands-ontraining of working
on sophisticated
equipments/
instruments
etc.
Stipend may also be provided
to such studenttrainees, sometime. After such industrial! on the job training, the student-trainee
goes back to his respective institution
for completion of the academic course.
3.
In such cases, it is made clear that employer employee relationship
does not exist between the industry and
student-trainee,
who is on industrial
on the job training
as an integral component
of a recognized
course of an
educational! technical institute recognized
by the Central! State Government
or any other authority constituted
by the
Central!State
Government.
Therefore,
the payment
of stipend,
if any, provided
by the industry
to such studenttrainees
do not attract the provisions
of the Employee
Provident
Funds & Miscellaneous
Provisions
Act,
1952.
However for the students getting placement
in companies
and appointed
as employees
of establishment,
Employee
Provident Funds & Miscellaneous
Provisions Act, 1952 will be applicable on such employees
even during on the job
training/induction/other
trainings taken after becoming employee.
4.
All concerned are advised to proceed in the matter accordingly.
(This issue with the approval
of CPFC)

Subject:- Conducting of ‘Nidhi Aapke Nikat'’ — regarding.
Sir,

Kindly refer to this office letters of even number dated 8.6.2015, 9.07.2015
and 6,08.2015 respectively on the subject matter in which comprehensive directions
regarding conduct of the programme were issued. However, while reviewing the
subject, Central PF Commissioner has expressed his displeasure at the way the field
offices have been reporting about the conduct of the programme. Inordinate delay
is Noticed in reporting the conduct of the programme. The consolidated report from
the ACCs (Zones) are being received in many cases, weeks after the due date which
is not at all acceptable. Central P.F Commissioner has expressed his unhappiness at
this lackadaisical approach.

Moreover, it is seen that despite the clear instruction from the Head Office,
some of the offices have not uploaded the details on the MIS Dashboard for the
purpose. This item of work should be ensured on top priority and there should be
no occasion where the office has failed to upload the detail on the dashboard.

It is once again requested to upload the report on the dashboard on the same
day or the next working day without fail as per the instructions of Head Office and a
consolidated report in the prescribed format may be sent to Head Office positively.

Further, on going through the reports on ‘Nidhi Aapke Nikat’, it is also seen
that the participation by EPF stakeholders has shown a downward trend and in some
offices, no participation is reported in August and September, Hence, instructions
have been given by Central P.F. Commissioner to ensure that:-

i} The number of employees representation should not be Jess than 30 in case
of Regional Office and 10 in case of Sub Regional Office.

li) The number of employers should not be less than 20 in case of Regional
Office and Sub Regional Office except in those cases where paying
establishment is less than 500,

iii) Similarly, 20% of exempted establishment must be called for interaction if
establishments are less than 100 and 10% if establishments are more than
100.

In view of the above, ACCs (Zones) are requested to take necessary action
accordingly and the desired reports on Nidhi Aapke Nikat programme must be
sent timely to Head Office.

[This issues with the approval of Central P.F. Commissioner.]

Yours faithfully,

Sub: Investments made by exempted trusts in recently downgraded companies
Advisory.

Sir,

The establishments exempted under Section 17(1)(a) and 17 (2) of the Employees”
Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 read with Para 27A of the
Employees Provident Funds Scheme, 1952 are required to follow the conditions as
delineated in Appendix ‘A’ to Para 27AA of the EPF Scheme, 1952.

2. The condition No.17 of the said Appendix stipulates that “7he Board of Trustees
shall invest the monies of the provident fund as per the directions of the Government from
time to time. Failure to make investments as per directions of the Government shall make
the Board of Trustees separately and liable to surcharge as may be imposed by the
Central Provident Fund Commissioner or his representative.”

3. Further attention is invited to condition No. 28 of the said Appendix ‘A’ that
stipulates “Jn the event of any loss to the trust as a result of any fraud, defalcation, wrong
investment decision etc., the employer shall be liable to make good the loss.”
Accordingly, the exempted establishments are supposed to recoup the loss incurred by the
trusts from its own source whenever there is any loss to the trust due to bad investments.

4, In this regard, it has come to notice that ratings of M/s. Amtek Auto, M/s. Jindal
Steel & Power Limited (JSPL) and some other companies have been downgraded in the
recent past. Accordingly, all the exempted establishments under your jurisdiction may be
advised to closely monitor companies in the Provident Fund portfolios of their respective
trusts that have been downgraded recently/likely to be downgraded in near future and
report deviation, if any, to this office at the earliest.

prepared carefully by keeping in view the requirement as well as the usual time taken in
obtaining administrative approval/sanction as well as the periodicity of releasing the
sanctioned amount

Continue..........

OFFICE MEMORANDUM

Subject : Grant of Dearness Relief to Central Government pensioners/family
pensioners - Revised rate effective from 1.7.2015.

The undersigned is directed to refer to this Department’s OM No. 42/10/2014P&PW(G) dated 27" April, 2015 on the subject mentioned above and to state that the
President is pleased to decide that the Dearness Relief (DR) payable to Central Government
pensioners/family pensioners shall be enhanced from the existing rate of 113% to 119%
w.e.f. 1 July, 2015.

2. These orders apply to (i) All Civilian Central Government Pensioners/Family Pensioners
{ii) The Armed Forces Pensioners, Civilian Pensioners paid out of the Defence Service
Estimates, (iii) All India Service Pensioners (iv) Railway Pensioners and (v) The Burma Civilian
pensioners/family pensioners and pensioners/families of displaced Government pensioners from
Pakistan, who are Indian Nationals but receiving pension on behalf of Government of Pakistan
and are in receipt of ad-hoc ex-gratia allowance of Rs. 3500/- p.m. in terms of this Department's
OM No. 23/1/97-P&PW(B) dated 23.2.1998 read with this Department's OM No. 23/3/2008P&PW(B) dated 15.9.2008.

3: Central Government Employees who had drawn jump sum amount on absorption in a
PSU/Autonomous body and have become eligible to restoration of 1/3"? commuted portion of
pension as well as revision of the restored amount in terms of this Department's OM No. 4/59/97P&PW (D) dated 14.07.1998 will also be entitled to the payment of DR @ 119% w.ef. 1.7.2015
on full pension i.e. the revised pension which the absorbed employee would have received on
the date of restoration had he not drawn lump sum payment on absorption and Dearness
Pension subject to fulfillment of the conditions laid down in para 5 of the O.M. dated 14.07.98.
in this connection, instructions contained in this Department’s OM No.4/29/99-P&PW (D) dated.
12.7.2000 refer.

4. Payment of DR involving a fraction of a rupee shail be rounded off to the next higher
rupee.

Subject: Online Registration of Establishments (OLRE).

Kindly refer to earlier instructions issued on 2.5.2014, 8.7.2014, 8.9.2014, 14.11.2014, 20.11.2014

and 30.12.2014. It has been reported that some offices have provided faulty information to the employers who
want to get the PF code.

2.

3.

In this regard, the following is made very clear:

The establishment can go on OLRE portal and can get their PF code online and at this stage, there is
no contact required with the office whatsoever.

The establishment can start remittances immediately as no document is required as a pre condition
for getting PF code or for depositing of the remittances.

The collection of the physical copies of the documents is a separate process altogether and is not
linked to the registration and the remittances. The employers will not be asked to come and hand
over the documents rather the Enforcement Officers will go themselves to collect the documents and
educate the establishments for further compliance.

Further the IS Division is upgrading OLRE Portal so that the establishments will be enabled to submit

digitally signed documents. When that happens, Enforcement Officers will no longer visit the establishment even

for the purpose of collecting the documents as mentioned in para 2(iii) above.

(This issues with the approval of CPFC)

FAQ on Exchange Traded Fund
Q1.
What is an Exchange Traded Fund?
Ans.
An exchange-traded fund (ETF) is an investment fund traded on stock exchanges. An
ETF may hold assets such as stocks, commodities, or bonds, and trades close to its net
asset value over the course of the trading day. Most ETFs track an index.
Q2. What is NIFTY based ETF?
Ans. NIFTY based ETF replicates NIFTY index of NSE. The investments are made in the
same stock and in the same proportions as in NIFTY index.
Q3. What is SENSEX based ETF?
Ans. SENSEX based ETF replicates SENSEX index of BSE. The investments are made in the
same stock and in the same proportions as in SENSEX index.
Q4. Who decides as to which shares are to be bought for NIFTY/Sensex ETF?
Ans. Shares are bought and sold only in the shares which are part of NIFTY or SENSEX. The
fund manager has no role in deciding which shares are to be bought in NIFTY / SENSEX
ETF. The constituents of the index are decided and changed periodically by the exchange
/ index manufacturer.
Q5. Who decides as to what proportion of any shares is to be bought in NIFTY /
SENSEX ETF?
Ans. Shares are bought and sold in the same pre – defined proportion of the index according to
their respective weightage. The fund manager has no role in deciding the inter se
proportion of shares to be bought in NIFTY / SENSEX ETF. The constituents of the
index and their proportion are desired and changed periodically by the exchange / index
manufacturer.

Sub: Furnishing of details required for Assessment and timely declaration
of Productivity Linked Bonus for the year 2014-15.

Sir,

Please refer to the above said subject. The work relating to the assessment of P.L.
Bonus for the year 2014-15 has been taken up by the Headquarters. Ministry of Labour &
Employment vide their letter dated 15th March 2013 instructed EPFO to review the new
PLB Scheme as the ‘Productivity Factors’ might have changed and directed to formulate a
fresh PLB Scheme and send the same after getting it recommended from the Executive
Committee, EPF. Accordingly, the work relating to review of Productivity Linked Bonus
Scheme for the employees of the EPFO has been entrusted to National Productivity
Council (NPC), A draft report on P.L. Bonus Scheme has been submitted by the NPC and
preliminary discussion has also been held in-house. As it may take some time in
formulation and getting formal approval of the Central Government, hence it has been
decided to collect the information from all Regions relating to assessment of P.L. Bonus
with reference to existing the P.L.B. Scheme as approved by Government of India in
December, 1999. Information relating to parameters and performance as per the Scheme
is to be furnished, as usual, in the Annexure A to C (Forms enclosed).

ACCOUNTS & CASH

2. During the year 2014-15, time-limit of 30 days (calendar days) was prescribed for
completing the job relating to settlement of PF, EPS and EDLI claims, Transfer cases and
cases pertaining to Advances. In case the job is not completed within 30 days, weightage
would be reduced to half for the work done beyond 30 days. Date of receipt of claim
form (complete in all respect) and the date of dispatch of cheque/transfer through NEFT
would be taken into account for reckoning 30 calendar days. In some of the cases, it
was found that the date mentioned on the cheque is taken into account, which is not
correct. The actual dispatch of cheque takes much more time after the cheque is
prepared and signed by the authorized officer. In order to avoid delay in dispatch, it has
been decided that. only the actual date of dispatch of cheque as recorded on the slip
issued by the post office should only be taken into account. In other cases where no
cheque is to be issued like PPO, Transfer out not involving actual transfer of PF

accumulations etc., the actual date of issue of PPO and the date of actual transfer will be
taken into account.

- 3. As regards issue of “Annual Statement of Accounts”, it has been classified into two
groups, Viz. (1) current year’s Accounts slips issued and (2) Previous year’s Accounts
slips issued during the current year. Accounts slips relating to the “current Year” and
those pertaining to previous years but issued during the current year should be shown
separately. The Number of accounts slips issued with the help of outside agencies and
the number of accounts slips prepared and issued on computers of EPFO may also please
be furnished separately in Column 9 of Annexure “A”.

4. Activity “issue of cheque against the PPO of Monthly Pension cases” has been
added in the Bonus scheme, 1999. Those beneficiaries who opt to get Monthly Pension
through their Bank Accounts are sent cheques from the Regional/Sub-Regional Offices
itself. This activity has been included in the PLB Scheme, 1999 with a view to encourage
the staff members to issue the cheques of Monthly Pensions as promptly as possible.
Accordingly, information may be furnished separately for all the three categories as
provided in Annexure-A.

ENFORCEMENT & DAMAGES
5. The activities of “Enforcement & Damages” include:

(1) No. of 7A notices issued.

(2) No. of Speaking Orders of 7A passed and compliance effected.

(3) No. of Speaking Orders passed for Levy of Damages.

(4) No. of Recovery Certificates Executed:-
(a) For default in all the five Accounts (A/c No. 1,2,10,21 & 22)
(b) For default in 3 or 4 of the five Accounts.
(c) For default in 1 or 2 of the five Accounts.

7-A NOTICES

6. Only one notice has to be taken into account for all the three Schemes. In case
three separate notices are issued for the three Schemes, it has to be taken as one only.
Further, only the initial notice issued has to be taken into account and not the notices
issued every time after adjournment of proceedings due to any reason. With the
amendment of Section 7A, the RPFCs are required to decide not only the quantum of
dues but also to decide the Applicability. In such cases also if more than one notices are
issued, it should be taken as one only for the purpose of PLB return.

year.

personal attention in assisting the Regional Commissioner in-charge of the
Region. Regional Offices may frame the BE/RE with due care as per provisions
in GFRs after assessing the actual needs of the regions. It has been observed
that in the last five years, RE was more than BE but the actual expenditure
was even less than the BE this is clearly a reflection of weaknesses in the
budgetary exercise. Further, RE may be projected in such a manner to obviate

the need for re- appropriation in the last quarter of the financial year.

Seeding of KYC by EPFO offices in respect of employers having employees

Sir/Madam,
It may be recalled that
EPFO has made it mandatory
for all the employers
having
employees more than 50 to have Digital Signature registered with EPFO to carry out various
digital verification
activities
including
KYC seeding. A number of representations
have been
received from various field offices for providing a functionality
for digital verification
of KYCs
by the field offices
in respect
of employers
with
less than
50 employees
which
are not
required to have digital signature as mandated by EPFO.
2.
Accordingly,
a functionality
has been provided to facilitate
the employers
with
less
than 50 employees to get their KYCs approved digitally by their concerned field offices. The
functionality
introduced
can be operated
by field offices by creation of authorized
users and
registering their digital signature on the OTCP portal. The choice of authorized
users is to be
made strictly in accordance with the instructions
issued earlier by Head Office vide its letter
No. IS 1(3)2003/Norms/8284
dated
11.09.2014.
All the field offices
are requested
to go
through
the
said
letter.
However,
a few
points
are
being
reiterated
for
the
sake
of
understanding
the functionality
as below:
•
The employer would upload the KYC on his own as detailed in User Manual and take
a print out of the member details with KYC. He shall verify the same by putting the
physical signature and seal of the authorized signatory and submit the same to EPFO
offices;
•
Upon receipt of these documents,
an APFC or any other officer not below the rank of
AO/EO authorized
by OIC shall verify these documents
before approving
such KYC

details on the UAN Portal. The verification
will be done using digital signature of the
officer so authorized, just as it is being done by the employer;
•
The storage of the KYC documents physically verified and submitted
by the employer
and subsequently
verified by APFC or any other officer so authorized
by orc on the
portal will also be important
for future
reference.
Therefore,
these KYC documents
may be scanned by the officer and uploaded on the UAN Portal for which necessary
facility
shall
be provided
on the
portal,
very
shortly.
As a matter
of abundant
precaution, the verified physical documents received are to be got hard bound by the
orc and stored safely for future
reference and retrieval as and when required since
the development
of the software is likely to take some time;
•
This facility shall be restricted to only in respect of those employers who on the date
of allotment
of UAN had 50 or less employees;
•
This facility
shall be enabled
by offices
on receipt
of specific
request
from
such
establishments.
3.
As explained above, the functionality
would require action at the end of employer as
well as field offices. The process flow has been explained in detail at Annexure. Accordingly,
it is requested
to
make
use of this
functionality
of
KYC details
in
respect
of smaller
employers that is with less than 50 employees and not possessing Digital Signature.

Subject: Payments through NEFT for EDLI benefits.
Sir/Madam,

Please refer to the above said subject.
2. At present, all the payments to the beneficiaries are made through NEFT (National

Electronic Funds Transfer) except for the payments from EDLI Account No.21 which are being
made through cheques.

3. It has been decided that payments from Account No. 21 may also be effected through
NEFT system to facilitate an efficient, secure, economical, reliable and expeditious payment
system. ROs/SROs may present individual cheques to the link branches of State Bank of India
(SBI) for NEFT payments. In case of payments for non-NEFT enabled banks, cheques may
continue to be sent through speed post. SBI, on receipt of the cheque, will credit the same to
the account of the beneficiary through CBS if the account is maintained in SBI or through NEFT
if account is in non-SBI bank. This interim arrangement shall be in place until a provision is
made in the software for the same.

4. Kindly take note that while making payments through NEFT/Electronic mode, no
revenue stamp would be required to be affixed on submission of claim forms by the
beneficiaries.

5. This has approval of Central P.F. Commissioner.
Yours faithfully,
(Sanjay Kumar)

Subject: Workshop for Representatives of Un-exempted Establishments from 29-30
September,2015- Inviting Nominations — Regarding.
Sir,

The National Academy for Training & Research in Social Security has been conducting
Workshop for the Unexempted Establishments on Employees’ Provident Fund and
Miscellaneous Provisions Act 1952 for the last several years.

The response for the programme from the industry has been quite encouraging and
almost all of the participants felt that such programmes should be conducted regularly to
inform the developments in EPF and EPS Administration.

As per the feedback of the participants in the earlier programs, and keeping in view
the recent developments in EPF and EPS Administration, the Academy has designed a two
day Workshop for Representatives of Un-exempted Establishments from 29-30 September,
2015.

During the workshop following issues will be discussed:

" Provisions of the EPF & MP Act, 1952 and the Schemes;

" Key issues posing challenges in compliance;

" Sorting out processes and procedures for better coordination and cooperation in
implementation of the Act & Schemes.

* Computerization in EPFO.

We request you to sponsor suitable number of Officers of your establishment for the
above workshop.

Keeping in view the requirement of Un-Exempted Establishments and their interest to
participate in the programme, we have kept the participation fee for Residential participant
@ Rs.5,000/- (Rupees five thousand only) per participant covering boarding and lodging,
course material etc. and Rs.4,000/- (Rupees Four Thousand only) per participant for those
not availing accommodation at NATRSS, they will be given study material and lunch.

The stay arrangements have been made for nominated person(s) in the campus of
the Academy from the evening of previous day i.e. 28.09.2015 and upto the next day
morning of the end of the programme i.e.01.10.2015.

Office Memorandum

Subject: Implementation of Suo Motu Disclosure under Section 4 of RTI Act, 2005

| Attention is invited to detailed guidelines on implementation of suo motu

| disclosure under Section 4 of RTI Act, 2005 issued vide this department's O.M.
No.1/6/20114AR dated 15.4.2013. Subsequently, a Committee of experts consisting of
Shri A.N. Tiwari, Chief Information Commissioner(Retd) and Dr. M.M.Ansari, Information
Commissioner(Retd) (of Central Information Commission) was constituted to
recommend, interalia, measures to further strengthen implementation of Section 4 of
the RTI Act, 2005. The Committee has, interalia, made the following recommendations
which have been duly accepted by the competent authority:-

1) All the details of the public authority may be uploaded on its website.
Access to information should be made user-friendly for which appropriate
information technology infrastructure should be suitably designed,
developed and operationalised.

2) All the training modules for professional upgradation of employees should
incorporate matter relating to the virtues of transparency and open
government and RTI flaw.

3) In order to minimise the burden of servicing RTI applications, the public
authorities with high public dealings should put in place an effective
system to redress the grievances of affected persons. At the suborganisational levels, there should be cooperation and coordination
between the Central Public Information Officers and the officers
responsible for addressing public grievances.

4) in order to reduce the number of RT! applications relating to service
matters, the information relating to recruitment, promotion and transfers
should be brought into public domain promptly.

5) The retention and maintenance of specific documents for specified
duration should be clearly spelt by each public authority in respect of its
documents.

Sub: Issue of summons for personal appearance of Employers — Reg.
Sir

Li

As per the provisions of the EPF & MP Act 1952, vide Notification No.S.0.1913 the Central
Provident Fund Commissioner, and all APFCs, RPFCs, Addl. CPFCs, have been notified as Inspectors
under Section 13(1) of the EPF & MP Act. All officers accordingly possess the powers of Inspectors
under the EPF & MP Act and can cause inspection of any premises and/ or summon such documents
and information as may be required for the purpose of enforcing the provisions of the Act. However, as
a matter of policy, the officers are confined to exercise their power as Inspector subject to the
geographical jurisdiction of the office where they function. This ensures that there is no interference /
overlapping of functioning between any two offices/ officers. Main task of officers at zonal offices and
Head Office is to administer and review the performance of the subordinate offices and not to exercise
above powers in routine.

Summoning of employer by officers at multiple levels will create confusion and unwanted
duplicity of work. It is therefore, decided that the officers in Head Office and Zonal ACC Office will not
summon employers directly for any purpose in exercise of powers delegated under Section 13(1) of the
EPF & MP Act and will normally use the services of officers in Regional/ Sub-Regional Offices for getting
the work done.. Wherever there is any special need for summoning any person directly, permission of
Additional Central Provident Fund Commissioner (HQ-Compliance) or Central Provident Fund
Commissioner shall be obtained for the same.

Sub: Dispensing with the procedure of affixing of Re 1/- Revenue Stamp on

2.
At present, Re 1/- revenue stamp has to be affixed on claim forms by members
for settlement of claims. The issue of continued practice of affixing of Re 1/- Revenue
Stamp on claim forms has been examined in consultation with the Ministry of Law &
Justice. It has been advised that while making payments through National Electronic
Funds Transfer (NEFT), no revenue stamp would be required to be affixed on
submission of claim forms by the members.
3.
Therefore, the practice of affixing revenue stamp on claim forms is discontinued

offices may procure a digital signatures (class 2 & above), so that the process may be implemented

Sub: Transfer Policy of Group ‘A’ officets of EPFO — reg.
Sit/ Madam,

As you may be aware, the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India (in its judgment dated
31/10/2013 in the Writ Petition (Civil) No.82 of 2011; T.S.R Subramanian & Ors. Vs.
Union of India & Ors.) had directed for transparency in the matters of transfer and
postings of officers and to ensure a fixed tenure of posting. It had also directed to
constitute Civil Services Board (CSB) to ensure fairness in these matters. Pursuantly,
instructions were issued by Department of Personnel & Training, Government of India
(vide the Meeting Notice and OM bearing number 11013/10/2013-Estt.A dated
December 26, 2013 and January 09, 2014) for implementation of the judgment of the
Supreme Court and to formally notify/circulate/publish in website these instruments
and to place them in the public domain.

2. Taking a cue from it, the EPFO drafted / formulated a Transfer Policy for the
cadre of P.F. Commissioners of all descriptions, on the lines of Civil Services Board
barring a few changes as pet requirement of EPFO. The said policy is being placed
before the Executive Committee of the Central Board in its ensuing meeting. After
approval, we shall be placing the policy on the website of EPFO.

3. Further, Regulation 5 of the Employees’ Provident Fund (Officers and
Employees’ Conditions of Services) Regulations, 2008 dealing with the subject of power

PTO,

to transfer is also being amended to bring it in synchronisation with the Transfer Policy

so far the CPFC alone had the powers to transfer as per powers delegated by
CBT/Govt.

Yours faithfully,

Authority to secure compliance from the establishments covered and coverable under
the EPF & MP Act, 1952 and manage default lies with the Regional P.F. Commissioners of the
Regional Offices and Sub Regional Offices. Exempted/Relaxed Establishments are no exception
to this. In case of establishments who are enjoying exemption/relaxation and maintaining their
own Provident Fund Trusts, one of the mechanisms to secure compliance and ensure default
management is through compliance audit of the establishments and the Trusts.

Z. It has come to the notice that some of the field offices have not been conducting
Compliance Audit of the Exempted/Relaxed Establishments falling under their territorial
jurisdiction in anticipation of issuance of directions from the Head office in this regard. Here it
is pertinent to reiterate that securing compliance and default management in respect of all the
establishments including exempted/relaxed establishments, covered under the EPF & MP Act,
1952 lies within the original jurisdiction of Regional P.F. Commissioners of the field offices.
Hence, they need not wait for issuance of directions from the Head Office in this regard.

3: Henceforth compliance audit of exempted/relaxed establishments should be conducted
by the Field Offices regularly on annual basis. Proforma of the compliance audit report has
already been circulated to the offices vide Head Office circular No- C-Ex/Misc./Comp.
Audit/2009/3124-31391 dated 10.10.2011 and is available on the official website of EPFO at Sl.
No. 342 under Office Orders/Circulars (2011-12) page.

Yours Faithfully,

i Same

(Rajesh Bansal)

Subject: Staff Grievance Handling System (SGHS) - regarding
Madam/Sir,

To streamline the system of handling internal grievances of serving and retired EPFO
Officers and Officials, a software namely “Staff Grievance Handling System” was put on
trial in December 2014. The online System is web based and can be accessed at

: r through the home Page tab Staff
Grievance Handling System in the “Logins” section.

Pension to the Pensioners. The grievance raised thus iS available for action at these
Offices in the first instance. The offices concerned can access posted grievances through
their login as SGHS role.

Following actions are expected by the offices:

1. Examine the grievance and resolve if the subject matter wholly relates to the
Originating office (Dispose with Final Reply)

2. Reject ineligible grievance citing appropriate reasons. For instance final reply can
be entered if the case has already been disposed.

3. Forward the grievance to another Office, if the issue pertains to other
jurisdictions. This can be done to one or multiple offices depending upon the
competency of the offices where the decision making lies. (Partially Forward)

4. The grievance can also be forwarded in Parts. This would be applicable to cases
that pertain to Login office as well as other office(s).

5. Interim reply, can also be recorded in case the final disposal is likely to take some
time.

STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE FOR
HANDLING PARLIAMENT QUESTIONS

The issue of furnishing replies to Parliament Questions(PQ) has
been reviewed and the following Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)
are being prescribed for handling the same:-
1. At the first instance the PQ Cell will gather information from print &
electronic media regarding the ensuing session of both Lok Sabha
and Rajya Sabha and collect a copy of formal notification of the
commencement of Parliament session. PQ Cell will then intimate
about the ensuing Parliament Session to all concerned Divisional
Heads.

2. The SS Division of Ministry of Labour & Employment have been
advised to send intimation about PQs and communications on
matters connected therewith by fax on 011-26100314 and by email
on rc.pqcell@epfindia.gov.in The Section Officer of PQ Cell shall
verify the email of PQ Cell on hourly basis from 9:30 a.m. onwards.

3. After the fax/e-mail is received in the PQ Cell, the SO (PQ) shall,
after making due entry in the Diary, take it to RPFC-II(PQ) in order
to specify which Division the Question pertains to. After the
questions are so marked the same will be served on the Divisional
Heads after taking acknowledgement along with date and time.
This activity shall be completed in not more than two hours after
the question is received in the PQ Cell.

4. The concerned Divisional Heads and other officers in the Divisions
upto the level of Section Officers shall regularly verify the website
of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha to ascertain the questions pertaining
to their respective Division.

5. If there is some confusion whether the question pertains to the
Division to which it is marked, the Divisional head shall ensure that
the same is returned to the PQ Cell immediately on receipt. Once
the PQ is so returned, the RC(PQ Cell) shall place it before the
ACC(PQ). In case the confusion is not sorted out the same should be
brought to the notice of CPFC for taking a final decision in the
matter. The entire process from the receipt of the Question and
the final conclusion of CPFC shall be completed within a span of one
hour.

6. After receiving the PQs, the Divisional Heads will collect the
required information including, if required, from field offices.
However, before making any reference to field offices Divisional
heads shall confirm, whether the information being requisitioned
from field offices is not already available in EPF Headquarters
through various periodic returns being furnished by field offices.
After due approval of CPFC, answers to the PQ should be submitted
to the PQ Cell.

Date: 28.07.15

Dear Commissioner,

The Universal Account Number (UAN) program has reached a very
critical stage in its life cycle and for it to attain its ultimate goal, employers
have a great responsibility in carrying out a number of activities for its
successful implementation. The most critical of the activities are dissemination
of UAN to the members, seeding of KYCs, completion of member details in
Member Master, confirmation of first time employment or previous employment
(Form 11) on UAN portal and encouraging the EPF members to activate their
UAN accounts. It is imperative upon the Field Offices to monitor these activities
and ensure that the envisaged benefits under UAN program are successfully
made available to all the EPF members.

Zs However, it has been noticed in the recent review meetings that most of
our officers in the Field Offices are still not fully aware of the processes
involved and the benefits that are available under the UAN program. You would
appreciate that monitoring and persuading the employers in our endeavor is
almost an impossible task if the EPF officers themselves are not fully seized of
the task at hand.

3. For a thorough understanding of the UAN program, the Field Offices are
advised to go through the user manuals available under UAN services. For the
convenience of one and all, video tutorials have also been placed on the EPFO
website. It is expected that all the officers in Field Offices would go through
these documents thoroughly. A matter should be referred to Head Office only
when a subject matter needs a higher level of intervention. Further,
suggestions and improvements in the material provided should be sent to IS
Division at epfo.project@epfindia.gov.in under intimation to the undersigned.

4. The seeding of KYC details of members in UAN database is to be
monitored by the field offices with special emphasis on Bank Account, PAN and
Aadhaar. In this regard, it may be noted that the district wise Aadhaar
saturation report for the entire country is placed at data.uidai.gov.in, which
may be used for monitoring purpose.

5. For better monitoring of the pending tasks, dashboards have been
provided to all the Field Offices. The facility of UAN based Member Master

download, which was earlier available to field offices through MIS portal, has
also been made available to employers recently.

6. It is reiterated that the purpose of UAN program is to bring the multiple
employments of a member under one umbrella id, identify the member through
his various KYC details, updation of Member Master in EPFO database and to
provide various e-driven facilities such as e-passbook, portability, SMS services
etc. to members. All these objectives are very crucial for establishing an
efficient and effective centralized system.

Ts I would therefore, sincerely urge each one of you to appreciate the above
concerns and put in your maximum effort to ensure that the UAN program is
implemented smoothly. I expect a regular feedback from all the ACCs in Zonal
Offices about the strategies being adopted to achieve the objectives and
suggestions for further improvements in the system and dashboards.

With regards,

Yours sincerely,

Sub: MA No. 469/2013 in OA No. 876/2013 filed by Sh. G Arjun Ranjan
Mangalore Bench, Bangalore Menial Munapal, SSSA, SRO, Shivamogga
Vs UOI & Others in the Hon’ble CAT, Bangalore Bench, Bangalore-reg.

Sir,

Sh. G. Arjun Ranjan Munapal, SRO (TBP), posted at SRO, Shivamogga opted for
voluntary retirement and had given notice on 16/08/2011 and requested the competent
authority to accept the same with effect from 01/09/2011. The competent authority
accepted the notice of voluntary retirement submitted by Sh. Munapal with effect from
01/09/2011 vide letter, dated 30/08/2011.

Thereafter, the applicant vide representation dated 15/09/2011, requested the
competent authority to withdraw the voluntary retirement order, dated 30/08/2011 as he
had not opted for voluntary retirement willingly but due to various compelling
circumstances. The competent authority, after examining the representation of applicant
with reference to rule provision, rejected the request for revocation of the voluntary
retirement order and informed the official through letter, dated 30/09/2011.

Agerieved by the said letter, the applicant has filed OA No. 876/2013 before the
Hon’ble CAT, Bangalore Bench seeking relief to set aside the abovesaid. The operative
part of orders, dated 16/04/2015 (Copy enclosed) passed by Hon’ble CAT, Bangalore

Bench, Bangalore is reproduced as under:-

“Heard. The applicant had given voluntary retirement application
vide Annexure A-1 requesting him to be relieved from duty w.e-f.

01/09/2011 after waiving off the normal waiting period of 90 days.
He would now rely on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the
case of Union of India and another Vs Wing Commander T.
Parthasarathy, reported in (2001) 1 SCC 158. In that case of Hon’ble
Apex Court had held that voluntary retirement can be withdrawn at
any time before the date which is assigned by the applicant therein as
his retirement date. But in this case, 15 days later than the date
assigned by himself and after acceptance of his retirement only had
the applicant claimed to withdraw the voluntary retirement
application. So the voluntary retirement application has become
concertized and final and therefore the Hon’ble Apex Court order will
not be applicable to the applicant. Therefore, there is no merit in the
OA. OA is dismissed.

This is for information please.
Yoursfaithfully,

Subject: Payment of Service Charge to pension disbursing banks — regarding.
Sir,

As you are aware that all pensioners under EPS, 95 are required to submit Life
Certificates/Non-remarriage certificate (LC/NRMC) in the month of November every year
through their respective pension disbursing banks. These certificates are required to be
forwarded by the Banks and updated in our application software for ensuring continued
disbursement of pension without any stoppage or breaks and to avoid any undue harassment

or problems for the pensioners.

2. In this regard, it is pertinent to mention here that under the banking
arrangements for pension disbursement the Banks have the onus for collecting and
forwarding LC/NRMC to EPF offices. However, it has been observed that LC/NRMC have not
been received in respect of many pensioners. It has also been reported by the field offices
that the service charges claimed by the banks are pending due to non-submission of LC/NRMC
by the disbursing banks and the pension disbursing banks are making references to
headquarters to release the pending service charges,

3.

The issue of payment of pension, receipt of undisbursed amount, release of

bank service charges and collection of LC/NRMCs has been considered and the following

instructions/guidetines are issued:

(i)

(ii)

(iii)

(iv)

(v)

(vi)

(vii)

(viii)

(ix)

Offices shall ensure that the BRS for release of pension in the subsequent month is
generated, verified and kept ready along with the softcopy file for releasing the
pension through CBS two days before the last day of the month.

The funds for releasing the pension payments should be transferred to the pension
disbursement bank account through NEFT/RTGS one day prior to the first day of the

subsequent month.

On the first day of the month the softcopy file for release of pension should be
presented by 10.30 a.m. in the pension disbursement bank branch. The pension
should be credited in pensioner’s bank account on the same day by the disbursing
bank.

The uncredited/undisbursed pension amount should be transferred to A/c No.10 by
NEFT/RTGS on the date of disbursement itself.

If the pension is not disbursed or the undisbursed amount is not credited back as
stipulated above, interest at the EPF interest rate as applicable on that date should

be claimed from the pension disbursement bank.

The undisbursed amount received back should be analysed and appropriate action
taken, If the account is closed then pension should be stopped through application
software and intimation sent to pensioner for intimating new account. The pensioners

for whom credit was not made should be properly updated in the application software.

The bank service charges should be paid in the month of January every year and that

too for pensioners whose life certificates have been received from the banks.

Bank wise branch wise list of pending life certificates should be provided to link branch
of pension disbursing banks as well as the respective branches with advise to obtain
the LC/NRMC for the pensioners by contacting the pensioner, In case of death the
same should be intimated to the EPF Office to update the system.

In case of death or if the LC/NRMC has not been received, then the excess amount
after the date of death or the date the LC/NRMC was due and not received should be
recovered from the account and paid back to EPFO,

Subject : Increasing interaction between EPFO and State Labour Department
and informing Regional Committees about new initiatives taken by
EPFO recently -- regarding.

Sir

The steps and the initiatives taken by Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation on
various core areas were discussed in the Regional Committee meeting of the State of Uttar
Pradesh under the Chairmanship of the Principal Secretary, Labour Department. It was
decided to issue instructions to various authorities of the State Government for ensuring
compliance to the provisions of the Employees’ Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions
Act, 1952 (the Act) and the Schemes framed thereunder. Accordingly, the instructions were

issued by the State Labour Department of Uttar Pradesh Government on the following
areas:

a) Compliance of the EPF & MP Act, 1952 by the Municipal Bodies.

b) Coverage of contractual Workers of Government, Semi-Government and State
Public Sector Undertakings.

C) Coverage of employees engaged in constructions units of Government, SemiGovernment and State Public Sector Undertakings.

d) Coverage of employees engaged in Sarv Shiksha Abhiyan.
e) Inspection of establishments jointly by EPF, ESIC and State Labour Department.

2. Similar action needs to be taken by the Labour Departments of various States. The
Additional Central PF Commissioners, In-charge of Zones and the Regional PF
Commissioner, In-Charge of Regions shall place all those issues pending with the State
Government, State Public Sector Undertakings, Semi-Government Bodies etc. before the
Regional Committee so that similar instructions are issued by the State Labour Department
which will ease securing compliance in respect of :

a) Contract workers working with various State Government Departments, State
Public Sector Undertakings, Semi-Government Agencies, Municipal Bodies etc.

b) Construction workers working with State Government Departments, State Public
Sector Undertakings, Semi-Government Agencies, Municipal Bodies etc.

c) Employees working in various Central/State run Schemes.

Page 1 of 2

3. EPFO has taken a number of e-governance initiatives like updation of member
accounts, viewing of member balance online, Online Transfer Claim Portal, Inoperative
Account Helpdesk, allotment and activation of Universal Account Number, Online
Registration of Establishments, payment of contribution by the employers through internet
banking, inspection of establishments through Shram Suvidha Portal, investigation of
complaints through Central Analysis and Intelligence Unit etc. for facilitating both employees
and employers. Additional Central PF Commissioners, In-charge of Zones and Regional PF
Commissioners, In-charge of Regions shall make it a point to put up an agenda on the
status of these initiatives before the meetings of the Regional Committee of the State
regularly.

4. Wherever the Regional PF Commissioner, In-charge of Regions experience difficulty
in activation of UAN by the employees working in State Public Sector Undertakings, SemiGovernment Agencies, Municipal Bodies etc., they shall impress upon the Regional
Committee for getting instructions issued by the State Labour Department for putting a
system in place for early activation.

5. In cases where the recovery of outstanding dues is held up in State Public Sector
Undertakings, Semi Government Agencies, Municipal Bodies etc., the same may be brought
to the notice of the Chairman of the Regional Committee who happens to be the Secretary
of the Labour Department of the State.

6. All the Additional Central PF Commissioners, In-charge of Zones and Regional PF
Commissioners, In-charge of Regions shall make it a point to report to Head Office the
important decisions taken in the Regional Committee for proper implementation of the
provisions of the Act and the Schemes framed thereunder.

7. You are aware that the Central Analysis and Intelligence Unit has already been
formed at Head Office which aims at collection and analysis of data for taking decisions to
ensure proper implementation of the provisions of the Act and the Schemes framed
thereunder. The Regional Committee is the appropriate forum where a decision can be
taken and appropriate instructions can be issued to various State Government departments

and Agencies for extending co-operation in sharing the data particularly in the field of
Labour.

Yours faithfully,

Sub: Social Security Agreement between Republic of India and the Republic of Austria.

Sir, ;
In pursuance to the Social Security Agreement (SSA) signed with the
Republic of Austria, the Government of India has now notified vide order No.
Ol-11012/03/2009-EP-Ii (Vol. H} dated 15-06-2015 that the above Agreement has
come into force with effect from 1° July, 2015. The text of the Agreement is
available on the official website of EPFO, www_epfindia.gov.in.

2. The agreement provides for detachment, totalisation and portability. Under the
detachment clause, the employees of one country deputed by their employers to
the other country on short-term assignment are exempted from Social! Security
contribution in that country up to a period of 60 months. However, such exemption
can be availed on the basis of “Certificate of Coverage.”

3. In view of above, concerned employee through employer may apply for
the “Certificate of Coverage” in the prescribed format (copy enclosed). Since the
“Certificate of Coverage” are to be issued by the RO/SRO, it may be ensured that on
receipt of the application complete in all respect, necessary action is taken by the
concerned RO/SRO for issuing COC in accordance with the consolidated guidelines
issued by the Head Office view letter No. |WU/7(15}2011/Gen (Software)/9209
dated 13-08-2013.

undertaken as per their entitlement

Sub:- Assessment of vacancies in the cadre of SSA in field offices-re-caste roster
year-wise from 2003-04 onwards-regarding.

Sir,

In order to initiate the process of recruitment for filling up of vacancies in the cadre of
SSA under DR quota, the number of vacancies as on 31/03/2014 and anticipated number of
vacancies as on 31/03/2015 in said cadre in prescribed proforma was called for vide Head office
letter no. HRM-IV/4(1)2015/SSA/DR/17464, dated 11/02/2015. On perusal of this information,
it were observed that some of the regions had shown the vacancies in OBC category which are
on higher side. However, in this context, the necessary guidelines were already issued to all
ACC (Zone) vide Head office letter, dated 12/09/2014 to ensure whether the reservation has
been applied in case of SSA (DR) from 03/01/2014 after adjusting all UDC’s against SSA post
(for which no reservation well apply). Most of the regions had not complied these directions

Therefore, it was decided to call for the concerned APFC (Admn), Liaison officer of the
region, Dealing Assistant who are well versed with the roster preparation above field offices
alongwith all relevant records related to assessment of vacancies in SSA cadre to verify the
vacancies in the cadre of SSA since 03/01/2004 i.e. the date of notification of recruitment rule
to the post of SSA. The said team had visited this office in April’15/May’15 and the process
how to finalize the roster was explained as per the following instructions issued by Head office
from time to time regarding preparation of post based roster in SSA cadre.

(i) Region-wise sanctioned strength of SSA communicated vide Head office letter no.
HRM-III/1(1)04/SSA/Pt. dated 27/02/2006 followed by subsequent allocation of additional posts
of SSA vide Head office letter no. HRD/1(7)99/Vol.III/Re-allocation of Group B & C/69723,
dated 26/12/2008 and surrender of posts on account of 10% matching saving vide Head office
letter of even no, dated 01/11/2010 (copy enclosed).

(ii) Necessary guidelines issued to all ACC (Zones) vide Head office letter no.
HRM/IV/4(1)14/SSA/DR/865, dated 12/09/2014 whereby it was directed to ensure whether the

reservation has been applied in case of SSA (DR) from 03/01/2014 after adjusting all UDCs
against SSA post (for which no reservation will apply)(copy enclosed).

Gi) It was clarified vide Head office circular no. HRM-III/1(4)2006/SSA/40002 dated
26/09/2008 that LDCs who have been prompted as SSA by passing skill test/examination etc
may be adjusted and shown against 15% Departmental Promotion quota. However, there may
be some imbalance in region-wise vacancies of Departmental Promotion quota. Some regions
may have excess Departmental Promotions and some may have excess Direct Recruitment for
the time being. This excess/shortage, however, may be adjusted against the overall sanctioned
strength of SSA and future retirement and promotion in higher cadre etc in the respective
office. Once the adjustment is made a cut of date has to be decided for operating the Direct
Recruitment and Departmental Promotion for categorization of future vacancies (copy
enclosed).

(iv) It was also reiterated to follow the instructions as per DOPT OM No. 14017/2/1997-Estt
(RR), dated 19/01/2007 regarding rotating the number of reserved posts in direct recruitment
quota and promotion quota in each year (copy enclosed).

This office has already explained all these things as mentioned above during the visit

~ of team of your region in Head office and also issued the instructions to the teams to send the

the rosters duly verified alongwith vacancy details at the earliest but the same has not been

received till date. It is, therefore requested to furnish the category-wise vacancy position in

provide the benefits for the same.

as envisaged under the Employee’s Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme, 1976.

Sir/Madam,

Please refer to the subject cited above.

2. Upon consideration of the proposals /justifications received from regions, the
competent authority in consultation with the Finance Wing of the Organisation, has
permitted to engage the manpower for data entry work on contract basis for the year 201516, subject to the following conditions :-

(i) The number of such DEOs must be restricted to the number hired in 2014-15,
however, under no circumstances, it should exceed 50% of the vacancies in the
cadre of SSAs as on 31.03.2015.

(ii) The offices which have proposed the requirement of lesser number of such
manpower than the number calculated as per sl. No. 2 (i) above must restrict to
the number whichever is least.

3. The Finance Wing has opined for reduction of expenditure on this head because of the
intake of SSAs recruited last year and also due to introduction of electronic receipt of returns
ete.

4. The ACC Zones are also requested to review the process of hiring of such manpower
especially where proposal submitted by the region appears to be on higher side when
compared to other offices.

5. Since the month of April - May 2015 have already passed, the RPFCs of the regions
are requested to adjust the expenditure incurred during this period into the overall limit as
mentioned above.

Contd...

6. Each Office shall follow GFR provisions and CVC instructions for selecting the vendor
for supplying of contractual manpower for data entry work.

7. It should however be ensured that the output of the manpower so engaged is
monitored timely and regularly and payment is made only after ensuring the minimum
required output from each person as per the norms for data entry work.

(This issues with the approval of CPFC)

Subject: Mandatory Deposit of Contributions through Internet Banking.

ii) HO Circular of even No. dated 22.06.2015

Sir/Madam,
Please refer to the above said subject.

2. The Central Government in exercise of the powers conferred by section 5 read
with sub-section (1) of section 7 of the EPF&MP Act 1952 has notified amendments in Paras
38(1) and 48 of EPF Scheme, 1952 making it mandatory for employers to pay the statutory
contributions through Internet Banking.

3. In exercise of powers conferred to the Central Provident Fund Commissioner
under amended para 38(1) of EPF Scheme, 1952, it has been allowed vide order of even No.
dated 24.06.2015 that an employer who makes payment of less than Rupees one lakh in a
particular month as contributions under Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous
Funds Act, 1952 and Schemes framed thereunder, shall have the option to make such
payments through bank drafts or banker’s cheques or cheques drawn only on the local bank as
was being done earlier. A copy of the said order is enclosed for information. This order shall
be valid upto the month of September, 2015. Thereafter, it shall be mandatory for all
employers to make payments electronically through internet banking. The employers
remitting contribution below Rs. | lakh per month shall, however, have the option to remit
such dues through the internet banking even during the interim period upto September, 2015.

4. The employers may be advised through e-mail/SMS/press release for
depositing contributions through Internet Banking as specified above.

ORDER

Ministry of Labour & Employment vide notification no. G.S.R. 360(E) dated
5h May, 2015 has amended Para 38(1) of the EPF Scheme, 1952. The Central
Government has made it mandatory for employers to pay statutory contributions
electronically through Internet Banking only.

2. In exercise of powers conferred to the Central Provident Fund Commissioner
under amended para 38(1) of EPF Scheme, 1952, it is hereby ordered that an
employer who makes payment of less than Rupees one lakh in a particular month as
contributions under Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Funds Act, 1952
and Schemes framed thereunder, shall have the option to make such payments through
bank drafts or banker’s cheques or cheques drawn only on the local bank as was being
done earlier. This order is being issued considering the fact that many of the
participating employers having smaller work force may not readily have facility of
internet banking.

3. This order shall be valid upto the month of September, 2015. Thereafter, it
shall be mandatory for all employers to make payments electronically through internet
banking.

(K.K. Jalan)
Central Provident Fund Commissioner

software
was launched in 2011, after that all modules viz. claim settlement,
annual account processing,
pension disbursement
and payment
is being handled
by this software.
Web based application,
normally
requires neither interruption
nor resubmission while processing (like
IRCTC, ONUNE-SBI etc. no refresh of page), as updation
of multiple
tables takes place during the
processing. This thumb
rule was not followed
by different
offices, leading to an inconsistent
state of
data. It is observed that the processing of a transaction
is very often interrupted
by refreshing
the
web page (pressing F5 key) due to which proper updation of all the data is not done.

A login facility
to
report
application
software
related
issues was given

the issue at their level

would
be sent to the NDC after
recording the steps that were taken in the field offices to resolve the issue.

due analysis. Even
those problems which can be resolved at their level like - file uploading issues/Incorrect
Input leading

version
need to be verified

offices.

Employer of the establishment covered under the Act is directed to get the declaration in
Form No. 14(New) from all the employees joining the establishment in a month and eligible
to become member of the Fund and upload the same in Universal Account Number (UAN)
Portal within 25 days of close of each month.

generated by EPFO to all his existing employees who are members of the Fund within 15
days from the receipt of UAN and get acknowledgement from them.

Employer of the establishment covered under the Act is directed to get the UAN activated
by his employees who are members of the Fund within 15 days of such dissemination.

details of such members (such as bank account details, PAN, AADHAAR etc.) within one
month of the receipt of UAN so as to enable them to avail the services from EPFO.

Numbers in respect of the members who have got AADHAAR within one month of
receipt of UAN. Wherever the members do not have AADHAR, the employer is directed to
obtain a certificate from such members of the Fund to the effect that they have no
AADHAAR within one month of receipt of UAN. As soon as the AADHAR is submitted
by any member, the employer is directed to upload the same on the UAN Portal within 15
days of receipt.

UAN and to seed all relevant information in the claim form before forwarding the same to
EPFO.

schedule prescribed above. Failure to adhere to the directions beyond wage month of September,
2015 will amount to non-compliance to the directions and the defaulting establishment shall be liable

Subject:- Launching of ‘Nidhi Aapke Nikat’ or ‘PF Near You" — regarding.
Sir,

1, Bhavishya Nidhi Adalat has been an important vehicle for grievance redressal in
EPFO for the past many years. Through these Adalats, EPF members were provided a
platfarm by which they could approach the office and could get their grievances
resolved, This initiative of the Organization has benefited countless subscribers. It is
equally true that with the changing times, adoption of IT enabled services and the
resultant improved service delivery mechanisms, the expectations of our subscribers
have undergone a sea change, Further, it needs to be acknowledged that employers
too are important stakeholders in the organization.

2: It Is, therefore, required that EPFO adopts a new form and structure to reflect
the changed ground realities as regards service delivery standards and rename the
Adalat ina way that would depict our commitment to all our stakeholders to provide the
best of services. By its very nomenclature, ‘Bhavishya Nidhi Adalat’ runs the risk of being
percelved as forbidding to the poor and underprivileged worker and therefore, he may
hesitate in approaching such an “Adalat” with its unsaid connotations of a courtroom

atmosphere, Therefore, after wide ranging consultations within the Organization, it has
dec to rechristen Bhavishya Nidhi i

3. This should, however, not be misconstrued a5 merely a name changing exercise.

As the name would suggest, it Is an endeavor on the part of the Organization to be

more accessible to its different stakeholders including employers and the programme

would serve to bring all of them on a common platform and facilitate exchange of ideas

and dissemination of information besides of course, grievance redressal. In other

words, EPFO will be moving away from a pure grievance redressal centered approach as

seen in Bhavishya Nidhi Adalat to a more broadbased and participatory approach in

| 0) 0 idhi Aapke Nikat. This would be in the nature of a publicity outreach programme the
Male toc of which shall be not only to redress the grievances of the subscribers but also
to invite their suggestions, enable employers to vent their grievances, if any, and to

sensitize the stakeholders at large about the multitude of new initiatives taken In their

interest by the organization,
te:

sf As was the case with Bhavishya Nidhi Adalat, Nidhi Aapke Nikat would be
conducted on the 10° of every month starting from July 2015. Incase the 10" happens
to be a holiday, the programme shall be conducted on the next working day. The
programme shall be held in every RO / SRO of the organisation and shall be presided
over by the Officer-in-Charge or in the absence of Officer-in Charge by the next senior
most officer. Sufficient publicity regarding the conduct of the programme should be
made before hand, preferably by the 20" of the preceding month through press releases
and communications to employers’ associations and trade unions to make it effective
and fruitful. Wherever possible, the employers can be informed through e-mail / SMS
also.

5, While inviting the participation of the trade union and employers associations,
they may be requested to convey any specific issue or grievance that they would like to
raise during the programme so that the office could be equipped to respond to such
queries in a quick and responsible manner during the programme. For effective conduct
of the Nidhi Aapke Nikat programme, it is mecessary that specific timeslots are
allotted to differant stakeholders.

6, It is suggested that the following slots will be in order:-

{i} Subscribers: 10:30 A.M to 1:00 P.M
(ii) Employers: 3:00 to 4:00 P.M
(iii) Exempted establishments located in jurisdiction: 4:00 to 5:00 P.M

Fi The above time slots are to be observed, but these are not sacrosanct.
Depending upon the culture of the area, different time slots can be determined by
