Sub: Strengthening grievance redressal mechanism & reiteration of instructions issued -
regarding.

Sur

On review of the grievance redressal position of the Organization, it is observed that
while there has been improvement in the rate of grievance redressal of various categories,
there is still ample scape for further improvement in the area of customer satisfaction so as to
minimize any sense of frustration or resentment which May arise in minds of EPF
members/pensioners who have very high expectations from us

It (8 therefore. imperative to use available mechanisms fo control and reduce the level of
members’ gnevances in order to ensure that our subscribers/members continue ta repose faith
and trust in our organization

Instructions have been issued by Head Office from time to time regarding the procedure
for receipt of grievances, thelr monitoring and disposal. However, it appears that instructions
issued vide this office circular no. CSD-VEPFIGMS/2014 dated Sth May 2014. circular no.
CSD-I/Visit Note/RO, Delhi -" SRO, Rohtak/2014/6183 dated of June, 2014. Circular no
CSD-VEPFIGMS/Action Plan/2014-15/7144 dated 24" June 2014 & circular no.
CSD-/Programme-Pragati/2015 dated 28°" Apnil, 2015 are not being followed consistently and

regularly

This is adyersely affecting the efforts being made to improve the image of the
Organization

Accardingly. its once again relterated that the procedure prescribed vide above circular
dated 5.5.2014 must be strictly followed. The responsibility mapping for all the tasks involved in
the process grievance handling is once again enclosed nerewith (Annexure/A) for strict
compliance

You are instructed to ensure that the time limits prescribed for each task are followed In
letter and spirit by each level of officers and staff responsible for handling and monitoring the
processes of grievanoe handling In field offices:

Further as earlier communicated vide this office circular dated 09.06.2014, all field
offices are instructed to pay special attention to the following Issues in their respective offices:-

+ All claims received elther by hand or by post In the offices, should be entered In the
system without any delay.

a in some cases, delay has been noticed in receiving back claim forms, which are referred
to the Enforcement Officer, for some clarifications/wanting documents etc. This delay
should be avoided Offices should sensitize the employers under their respective
jurisdiction to comply with the provisions of Para 72 of the EPF Scheme, 1952, wherein
the employer is duty bound te obtain the claim form duly filled in fram the ex-employee
on exit from-employment and to forward attested claim application to the respective
EPF Office within five days of receipt. If employer is found to be guilty of not obtaining
ihe filled in claim form from the ex-employees repeatedly even after many advisories
action may be initiated against the employer concerned

+ lt is observed thal often claims are returned! rejected on miner or flimsy grounds
Objections in piecerneal should be avoided. |n cases of Rerun/Rejection at the level of
Accounts Group, proper reasons for rejection should be selected in the application
software and the general practice of choosing “Other “ option as the reason should be
avoided, except in exceptional cases. The letter for return/rejectian of claim should be
generated fram the system

- Each Office should identify large Establishments submitting claims in bulk and conduct
meetings! workshops, where representatives of these establishments dealing with EPFO
related matters should be invited for discussion. They should be guided about the
proper procedure for filling and filing of various types of claim forms. so that claims
complete In all respect as per the eligibility of the member Is received. The common
reasons for returnrajection should also be discussed to minimize retum/rejection ratio.

Central Provident Fund Commissioner in many of his previous review meetings has
raised his concern about the pending Annexure K issue in many of the offices in India.
Circulars have been issued on several of the previous occasions as to how to handle Annexure
K which is wrongly received in office.
2.
For simplicity the wrong receipt of Annexure K is divided into two periods namely:
a)
Annexure-K wrongly received by transfer-in office after implementation of Online
Transfer Claim Portal (OTCP).
b)
Annexure-K received by transfer-in office for the period prior to the implementation of
Online Transfer Claim Portal (OTCP).
3.
In order to reiterate the process in simple terms, the following instructions which are
extract of the earlier instructions are being brought to the notice for immediate
implementation:-
a) Annexure-K wrongly received by transfer-in office after implementation of
Online Transfer Claim Portal (OTCP):
As you are aware that in all the cases where digital claims are being filed or physical
claims are being filed in transfer-in office which in turn is digitised. There is no present
complaint relating to wrong Annexure-K.
However, instances have been brought to
the notice of the Head Office where Annexure-K has wrongly been forwarded. These
cases are reported to be on account of wrong or non-updated mention of PF code by
the claimants. This PF code is being verified by the Dealing Assistant of the transferout office and is, therefore, being forwarded to wrong office. It is again brought to
your notice that it is the responsibility of the DA portal to verify the correctness of
transfer-in office before Annexure-K is forwarded to any office. The detailed process
relating to the roll of DA portal has been elaborated in H.O. letter No. IS/Project-I/
Transfer Claims/12573 dated 3rd October, 2013 and has been reiterated vide H.O.
letter No. R-I/Transfer Claims/Project-I/34724 dated 21st January, 2015 and H.O.
letter No. IS/R-I/Transfer Claims/Project-I/42580 dated 13th March, 2015.
You are
hereby once again requested to go through the provisions and strictly adhere to the
same in order to obligate the possibility of wrong forwarding of Annexure K in future.

b) Annexure K received by transfer in office in any period prior to
implementation of Online Transfer Claim Portal (OTCP): Majority of the
instances of pending Annexure K relate to this category. In all these cases, though
money has been received from the transfer-out office to the office, but the employer
and as a corollary, the member employee does not belong to the office. After release
of pending establishments, the possibility that the employer belongs to current office
has also been taken care of.
4.
In all these pending cases mentioned in para 3 (a) and 3(b) above, the Annexure-K
along with the amount wrongly received as transfer in has to be reverted to the transfer-out
office.
5.
The above process may be implemented meticulously and immediately. It is expected
that by the time, the issue is again reviewed in the next ACCs meeting, there will be no
pending Annexure-K in your zone.

Subject : Complaints likely to fall under the purview of CAIU — Mode and

Sir,
This is with reference to this office circular letter dated 01.09.2014 (placed at
official website of EPFO at Si. No. 407 of the Office Orders and Circulars

segment) wherein the mode and mechanism of transmitting complaints to CAIU by field
offices for the purpose of according permission to carry out inspection were prescribed .

2. All the Regional PF Commissioners In-Charge of Regional/ Sub-Regional Offices were
clearly instructed to transmit the complaints to CAIU in soft form only in the dedicated email, complaint.caiu@epfindia.gov.in. Despite clear-cut instructions, this office has been
receiving requests for permission to carry out inspection in physical form from a number of
offices, which results in avoidable and unnecessary paper-work and which is not cost
effective also.

3. Further, during the review meeting taken by Central PF Commissioner on 16-17"

Sub: Guidelines to be observed while sending suppiementary/additional budget
proposals to Head Office.

Sir/Madam,

It is imperative to bring to your notice that allotment of budget is not an endless,
on-going excercise. The field offices are obliged to incur only the expenditure duly
sanctioned by the competent authority, subject to availability of budget as per
allotment of BE/RE by the Head Office.

2. However, it has been noticed that some of the, offices send requesis for
additional allotment of budget immediately after receipt of BE/RE on the plea that the
offices had forgotten to include items in their proposals. In a few cases, even when
sufficient budget is available to meet out the existing requirements a proposal is sent by
the field offices.
1) It has been seen that the request for grant of ex-post facto sanction / ratification /
re-appropriation/ additional allotment of budget under certain budget heads does not
contain any justification and details regarding actual expenditure incurred upto date
that are necessary for placing the proposal before the competent authority in Head
Office.
H) In many cases, these requirements are not sent under the signature of RPFC-I of
the Region. The budget available in Sub Regional Offices is not considered af times.
3. As such before sending any request for additional allotment to Head Office, the
concerned Regional Office needs to ensure the following:-

1) References for ex-post facto sanction / ratification /re-appropriation/ additional

allotment of budget should be self contained with full justification and details regarding

-2actual expenditure incurred upto date etc. and forwarded under the signature of
RPFC-I| of the Region / Director, NATRSS/ Registrar, EPFAT only. The proposals may
be annexed with the last expenditure return no. li.

ft) As regards budgetary matters, only Regional Offices should take up the
matter with Head Office. It is seen that some SROs/ ZTls refer such matters to Head
Office directly. This practice may be discontinued with immediate effect.

it) Any unforseen expenditure over and above the sanctioned budget on
account of the visit of Parliamentary Committee, Rajohasha Committee etc.
opening of offices, the expenditure may be incurred from the sanctioned budget
only. In case the available budget is insufficient to meet the expenditure then the
Regional Offices may send a proposal alongwith the updated expenditure
statement.

IV) Kindly take note that the role of Finance Wing is limited to make availability
of budget and therefore, field offices may not send proposals for sanction or
approval to the Finance Wing. The approval may be obtained by the
concerned Offices from authorities competent to sanction the same.

V) The above instructions may be complied with by all the field offices.

Yous faithfully,

(SANJAY KUMAR)
Financial Advisor & Chief Accounts Officer

oir,

As the Universal Account Number (UAN) is allotted to the members on the
basis of Electronic Challan cum Return (ECR), a number of references have been
received from various exempted establishments for allotment of UAN to the new
members of exempted establishments who have joined after 01/09/2014 and
where the wages are more than = 15000. As such members are excluded from
Employees’ Pension Scheme, 1995, their names do not appear in the ECR and
hence they are not allotted UAN in the normal process.

Rs For allotment of UAN to such members, a functionality has been made

available to the employers. The broad features of the functionality are as follows:

e The Employer would upload a text file which contains the details of
exempted members’ member IDs through a facility available on OTCP
employer portal.

e Before uploading the text file, the system would carry out the following
validations that:

» These member IDs do not exist in OTCP member master.
= UAN have not been generated earlier for these member IDs.
» None of these member IDs are pending for new employment

confirmation on Employer portal.

3.

"None of these member IDs are uploaded by this exempted
establishment earlier.

« Date of joining is on or after ist September, 2014.

" The wages are greater than = 15000.

" The age is to be more than 58 years if the date of joining is on or after
1st September, 2014 and the wages are not greater than = 15000.
When file validation is successfully done, the system would generate a
tracking id and a PDF file which is to be digitally signed and approved by the

employer.

After PDF file is digitally signed by employer, the submission process is
complete.

The portal would send this Data to EPFO office (i.e. NDC) for UAN generation.
EPFO office (i.e. NDC) would generate the UANs and send the response file to
the portal.

These UAN will be updated in UAN master (with another flag for identification
of such UANs generated on request by exempted establishments)

The system will process the response text file and generate a PDF file
containing member ID, member name, UAN for dissemination to members
through employers.

The detailed process flow, along with screen shots, are enclosed herewith at

Annexure. All the field offices are requested to take note of this facility and guide

the employers to avail this facility to ensure that all such members also get the

Universal Account Number.

Sub:
Amendment in Section 192A of the IT Act, 1961- Instructions for deduction of
TDS on withdrawal from PF.
Ref:
Head Office circular of even number dated 18.03.2015.
Sir/Madam,
The Finance Act, 2015 (20 of 2015) has inserted a new section 192A regarding the
payment of accumulated provident fund balance due to an employee. The provision shall take
effect from 1st June, 2015. A copy of the said provision is enclosed for information.
2.
Income Tax shall be deducted at source (TDS) at the following rates if at the time
of payment of the accumulated PF balance is more than or equal to Rs. 30,000/-, with service less
than 5 years:-
3.
a) TDS will be deducted @ 10% provided PAN is submitted. In case Form No. 15G or
15H is submitted by the member, then no TDS shall be deducted.
b) TDS will be deducted @ maximum marginal rate (i.e. 34.608%) if a member fails to
submit PAN (and no Form No 15G or 15H).
TDS shall not be deducted in respect of the following cases:-
•
Transfer of PF from one account to another PF account.
•
Termination of service due to ill health of member, discontinuation/contraction of business
by employer, completion of project or other cause beyond the control of the member.
•
If employee withdraws PF after a period of five years of continuous service, including
service with former employer.
•
If PF payment is less than Rs. 30,000/- but the member has rendered service of less than 5
years.
•
If employee withdraws amount more than or equal to Rs. 30,000/-, with service less than 5
years but submits Form 15G/15H along with their PAN
A flow-chart is appended for understanding the implications of the amended provisions in the
Income Tax Act, 1961.

4.
Kindly take note that TDS is deductible at the time of payment of provident fund in
Form No. 19. Form No. 15H is for senior citizens (60 years & above) while Form No. 15G is for
individuals having no taxable income. Form 15G & 15H are self-declarations and may be accepted
as such in duplicate. Form 15G and 15H may not be accepted if amount of withdrawal is more
than Rs. 2,50,000/- and Rs. 3,00,000/- respectively. Members shall quote PAN in Form No.
15G/15H and in Form No. 19. The field offices may purchase pre-printed Form No. 15G & 15H to
assist the members in filling up Form No. 19.
5.
The process for authorization of Form No. 19 shall be as per the existing system.
However, wherever TDS has to be deducted @10%, the same may be approved on Form No. 19
by the APFC (Accounts). Wherever the TDS has to be deducted @34.608%, the same may be
approved on Form No. 19 by a RPFC level officer. These instructions shall apply in initial stages of
implementation of the amended income tax provisions. Since the members may not be aware of
the new provisions, therefore, it shall be the responsibility of SSA (Accounts) to communicate the
same to the member on telephone and record the same in Form No. 19 to submit PAN, Form No.
15G/15H, if applicable. A system generated statement of Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) may
invariably be sent to the member.
6.
Members who have rendered continuous service of 5 years or more, including
service with former employer, shall not be required to submit PAN and Form No. 15G/15H along
with Form No. 19. Similarly, members whose service has been terminated due to his ill health,
contraction or discontinuance of business of employer or other cause beyond the control of the
member shall not be required to submit PAN, Form No. 15G/15H alongwith Form No. 19. In such
cases, no income tax (TDS) shall be deducted in terms of Rule 8 of Fourth Schedule to the
Income Tax Act, 1961.
7.
The field offices shall deposit the Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) and returns
thereof by 7th of the following month. The existing TAN number obtained the respective offices
may be used to deposit tax to the local income tax authority. The in-house responsibility for
deposit of tax and returns thereof shall lie with Drawing & Disbursing Officer (DDO) as per the
existing system. The concerned officers and staff may be given an in-house training for
implementation of new provisions and RPFCs may engage CAs, who are on our panel.
8.
The above should be made applicable with effect from 01.06.2015 and all steps
should be taken before hand such as procuring copies of Form 15G and 15H. In case of any
clarification, the same may be escalated to the Head Office.

Subject: Implementation of Jeevan Pramaan — Aadhaar based Online
Pensioners’ Digital Life Certificate for pensioners under EPS, 95
— regarding.

Sir,

As you are aware that the Hon'ble Prime Minister has recently launched
“Jeevan Pramaan” — an “Aadhaar-based Online Digital Life Certificate” for pensioners,
a move that was aimed towards self-certification for pensioners in Central, State and
other Government entities. Under this initiative a pensioner can digitally provide
proof of being alive to authorities for continuity of pension every year instead of
requiring to present oneself physically or through a Life Certificate issued by specified
authorities. The present system requires that the pensioner has to submit a physical
life certificate to EPFO directly or through pension disbursement agency i.e, bank.
This exercise is to be carried out annually in the month of November to establish that
the pensioner was alive in order to ensure continuity of his pension. The proposed
digital certification will do away with the requirement of a pensioner having to submit
a physical Life Certificate in November each year to the pension disbursement bank
branch. The proposed system makes use of Aadhaar-based Digital Life Certificate for
pensioners. The pensioners are required to have Aadhaar number to make use of this
facility.

2. For the purpose, Department of Electronics and Information Technology
(Deity) and National Informatics Centre (NIC) has developed a software for

registration of pensioners under Central Government Schemes, etc. and further on
request of EPFO, NIC had carried out modifications in the software developed by
DeitY to differentiate the category of pensioners under EPS, 95 pensioners. The NIC
team for the project has developed a software utility that can run on personal
computers and Android operating system based smartphones. The software can be
easily downloaded from the web and used in conjunction with a USB fingerprint/Iris

device for Aadhaar based authentication.

3. After discussions on implementation and technical aspects with NIC,
the pilot implementation of the project was launched in the offices of Regional
Offices, Delhi and Chandigarh which has been successfully completed. As part of the
trial run both the offices carried out approximately 9000 registrations for Aadhaar

based online pensioners’ digital life certificates from following locations: i.e.

(i) Designated Jeevan Pramaan Centres in the Region: The
pensioner will visit Jeevan Pramaan center with his Pension Payment Order
and valid Aadhaar Card for registration and submission of digital life

certificate.

(ii) EPFO offices : The facility of registration will also be provided by the
respective offices. The office will install computer system and biometric
mechine for the purpose of registration and submission of digital life

certificate.

(iii) Branches of pension disbursing banks having maximum numbers
of pensioners: At this level, 4-5 branches of pension disbursing banks
may be identified having maximum number of pensioners. The respective
office will depute manpower in these branches with necessary system
support i.e computer and biometric mechine for registering the credentials
of the pensioners. In this regard, pensioners who have already submitted
the physical life certificates to banks are also to be contacted and

motivated to come for registration in these designated branches.

4. The status of the project and its further implementation in all the field
offices of EPFO was discussed in the meeting of ACCs(Zones) held on 16.4.2015 at

EPFO headquarters wherein it was decided to roll out the project in all field offices of

and are in receipt of ad-hoc ex-gratia allowance of Rs. 3500/- p.m. in terms of this Department's

3. Central Government Employees who had drawn lump sum amount on absorption in a

pension as well as revision of the restored amount in terms of this Department's OM No.
4/59/97-P&PW (D) dated 14.07.1998 wil will also be entitled to the payment of DR @ 113% w.e.f.
1.1.2015 on full pension i.e, the revised pension which the absorbed employee would have
received-orr the date of restoration had he not drawn lump sum payment on absorption and
Dearness Pension subject to fulfillment of the conditions laid down in para 5 of the O.M. dated
14.07.98. In this connection, instructions contained in this Department’s OM No.4/29/99-P&PW
(D) dated. 12.7.2000 refer.

4. Payment of DR involving a fraction of a rupee shall be rounded off to the next higher
rupee.

for immediate disposal. To ensure that no grievance remains un-disposed
after 30 days of its receipt, henceforth the following procedure may please be
followed Invariably:

8) Eorwarding of new/wrongly received grievances:-

grievance js resolved within 30 days.

following drill has to be followed:-

ti} All ACCs (Zanes) & ACC, Hgrs. must immediately review in case that remain

steps to ensure disposal.

and thé letter No. and the date shall be clearly mentioned In the interim ATR in

division in Head Offica and if need be may place such cases for consideration &
intervention of CPFC.

responsible to put in requisite system as above and make official/officers dealing with
grievance cases habitual of following above mentioned procedure.

disposal of grievances on dally basis so as to ensure that the Hon'ble Prime Minister
remains satisfied with the performance of EPFO in the area of redressal of grievance

Sub: Levy of Damages U/S 14 B - Discretion to vary rates of damages — reg.

Ref: Your Letter No. 14068/EPF/SRO/GKP/Legal dated 07-04-2015

Sir,

Please refer to your letter cited above. The matter has been examined and the
views of Head Officé are provided below.

2. _ It can be seen that the Section 14B of the EPF & MP Act, 1952 provides that the
Commissioner may recover frorn the employer by way of penalty such damages not
exceeding the amount of arrears, as may be specified in the Scheme. Since the Act
clearly specifies that the levy of damages shall be as specified in the Scheme, the rates
specified under the EPF Scheme 1952 under Para 32A shall be adopted without any
deviation. It is therefore clear that the Act does not provide any discretion on the Inquiry
Authority for varying the rates of Damages to be recovered from the defaulting employer.
The EPF Scheme 1952, under Para 32B, separately provides for reduction / waiver of
damages levied as per which the Central Board, EPF is empowered for the purpose.
Therefore the Employer aggrieved by the order of levy of Penal Damages has to
approach the Central Board of EPF for reduction / waiver of the same. The CBT will then

consider the case on merits separately subject to the provisions of thé EPF & MP Act
1952 and the Schemes framed thereunder.

3. It can be spen that the Authority levying Penal Damages under Section 14B of the
EPF & MP Act, 1952 shall provide an opportunity of hearing to the party concerned for
meeting the requirernents of the law of principles of natural justice. The requirements of
the principles of law of natural justice is that all the parties cOh¢érned shall be provided
with an opportunity to present their case before a decislon against their interest is taken.

In the' case of levy of pena! damages, issues to be considered are, whether there is a
delay in remittance, whether the delay stated in the notice is correct, whether the delay
is due'to.some situation beyond the control of the employer like disruption to normalcy of
public life due to disturbance like natural calamities, strike, bandh, etc. In such cases
where the delay is @m% due to situation stated above, the authority can consider and revise
the amount / date. -

4, Since there are two different authorities specified for two different purposes under
the law ie. for levy of damages and for reduction / waiver of damages, the authorities
cannot interfere witht one another's powers for the sake of regularity in the action

5. lt is therefore opined that the above may be placed before the Court for
consideration and the court can be informed that since the power to reduce or waive
damages is available at a different level the employers aggrieved by the PD Order can
approach such competent authority for consideration after the damages are levied by
inquiry authority and tere is no need for inquiry authority to exercise the same power.

This issues with approval of ACC (Compliance).

2. This issue was also deliberated in the meetings of the Standing Committee of
Parliament on Labour from time to time. A meeting was also taken up by Central PF
Commissioner where Senior Officers from BSNL, Head office and the President of the BSNL
Casual and Contract Workers Federation were present. During the course of discussion, the
Officers present in the meeting from BSNL assured that they will advise their Circle Offices
spreading over the country to report compliance in respect of both Casual Labourers directly
engaged by BSNL from the date of its formation i.e. from 01.10.2000.

3. Subsequent to that the General Manager, BSNL has submitted the Telecom Circle
wise number of such Casual Labourers having Temporary Status Mazdoor (TSM) totaling to
3469 which is enclosed herewith for ready reference. Most of these Casual Labourers have
been in engagement since the time of Department of Telecom and continued to be engaged
by BSNL after its inception on 01.10.2000. In the case of some of these workmen, the EPF
contribution has not been paid by BSNL for the period from 01.10.2000 or from the date of

their engagement up to 10.01.2011.

Subject : Declaration of result of Third Assistant Provident Fund Commissioner { Probationary}
Examination held from 19" January 2015 to 23rd January, 2015 —reg.

Sir,

Please refer to this office circulars dated 12.12.2014 (website sl n0651) regarding the conduct of
the Second APFC (DR) Prodationary examination held at NATRSS 19" January 2015 to 23rd January ,
2015.

a As per the EPF (Probationary) Examination Scheme, General Category candidates have to obtain
minimum 45 % marks in each paper and $C/ST Category candidates have to obtain minimum 40% marks
in each paper to pass the Probationary Examination. Thus candidates who are absent in even one paper
or those who do not get the minimum qualifying marks in even one paper are considered as ‘FAIL’ in the
éxamination and wiil have to appear for the same again. However candidates wha have failed to qualify
in the examination but have secured 50% and above in any one of the papers will be granted exemption
In that paper and will not have to appear in that paper In the next examination.

4, The result of the examination has been prepared as per the above Scheme and is enclosed for
Information of all and is subject to outcome of changes due to re-totailing and verification of marks etc,
Those candidates wha have failed in the examination and are required to appear for ane or more papers
may be directed to attend the next Probationary Examination, it is requested that all the concerned
candidates may be intimated about the result and directed to appear for the Third Probationary
Examination when the same is conducted.

4, As per the EPF (Probationers’) Examination Scheme, 1997, [ as amended from time to time}
enclosed with circular dated 09.05.2014 ( website circular no. 103), facility is provided for candidates
who desire retotalling of their marks and verification of the fact that all the answers written by them

SUBJECT: SUBMISSION OF ANNUAL IMMOVABLE PROPERTY RETURN FOR THE YEAR 2014
(ENDING 31.12.2014) BY GROUP 'A' AND GROUP 'B' OFFICERS UPLOADING THE
SAME IN PUBLIC DOMAIN— REGARDING.
In accordance with the instructions contained in MHA, O.M. No. 25/10/55
-
Estt. (A) dated 12
th January 1956, every government servant holding a Group 'A' or Group
'B' post is required to submit the immovable property return in prescribed format in respect
of every calendar year by 31 st January of the next year. Further as per Rule 18(1) (ii) of
CCS(Conduct) Rules, 1964 applicable to EPFO it is mandatory for all Group 'A' and Group 'B'
officers to submit their Annual Immovable Property Return.
2.
It has however been noticed that many officers are not submitting the
Annual Immovable Property Return within prescribed time limit. As per G.I. DoPT O.M. No.
11013/12/93-Estt. (A) dated 24.01.1994 strict action may be taken against employees who
fail to submit the returns in time or furnishing wrong information separately. This has
caused denial of Vigilance Clearance Certificate by the Administrative Vigilance Section
(HRM) / Vigilance Wing, Head Office, EPFO leading to blocking of career progression.
3.
Keeping in view the absence of any specific / clear directions to submit AIPR
by 31.01.2015 to HRM, EPFO instead of Region subsequent to direction containedd in this
office letter No.HR/AVS/PR/II/Misc./2011-12 dated 27.12.2012 that the offic
submit AIPRs to concerned RPFC's and who will in turn consolidate and forward all the
AIPRs' by 08th Feb. of the concerned year, as an interim measure it has been decided to give
one time relaxation regarding the last dated of submission of AIPR for the year 2014 (assent
on
01.01.2015) and to extend the same as to 30.04.2015. A written displeasure is being
separately to each of the Group 'A' officer who has not submitted the Annual Immovnote
able
Property Return in time. Similarly, the Zonal ACC are requested to issue a displeasure
Sir,

to each of the Group 'B' officer who has not submitted the Annual Immovable Property
Return in time.
4.
It is further cautioned that the officers who have not submitted the AIPR for
2014 so far may loose their vigilance clearance for promotion or empanelment or for
gratuity retirement dues in 2015-16 calendar year, if they fail to submit their AIPR for the
year 2014 by 30.04.2015. As per DoPT's O.M. No. 11012/112007 Estt. A dated 27.09.2011
and MoL&E circular No C-290201/12011 -vig. Dated Jan, 02, 2012 they may lose their
vigilance clearance
5.
Pending provision of online submission of AIPR, the RPFC-I Incharge of the
Region shall consolidate and forward all the AIPRs alongwith a list of defaulting officers on
day to day basis through mail and also through post copy so as to reach the mail and
scanned copy in HRM(AVS) on the same day. The officers shall also send a scanned copy
submitted to RPFC on the date they submit it concerned RPFC additionally hereafter to RPFC
(AVS)/ACC (HR) also so that any ambiguity on date of submission does not arise. A
compliance report on the above may kindly be forwarded via e mail to:
rc.hrmPepfindia.gov.in

Sub: Release of Pension under EPS-1995 without the Minimum Pension of Rs.
1,000/- per month from the Month of April 2015 onwards -‘Generation of

BRS for the Month of April 2015 only after receiving patch from IS
Division - Reg.

Sir,

As you are aware, the Government of India had issued the Gazette
Notification GSR No 593(E) dated 19.08.2014 providing for a minimum pension of
Rs. 1,000/- per month under EPS-95. As per the notification the provision of
minimum pension of Rs. 1,000/- per month in_ respect of
member/widow(er)/disabled/nominee/dependent parents and Rs.250/- per month and
Rs.750/- per month for Children and Orphan pension respectively was made
effective from 01.09.2014 and was specifically limited to the financial year 2014-15.

2. Consequent to the notification, appropriate changes in the application was
carried out by the IS Division and offices have disbursed the monthly pensions with
the minimum pension provision as provided for in the notification from the month of
September 2014 to March 2015.

3. While the matter has been referred to the Government for a decision on the
continuation of the minimum pension provision beyond 2014-15, a direction is yet
to be received. Under the circumstances EPFO cannot go beyond the directions of
the Government and the provisions of the Gazette Notification GSR No. 593(E)
dated 19.08.2014 and the payment of pension from the Month of April 2015 will be
released at earlier rates i.e. without the minimum pension provision.

4, All field offices are, therefore, directed to ensure that the BRS processing
cycle for the month of April 2015 for credit of pension in May 2015 should only
be carried out after receiving the necessary patch from IS Division.

5. The directions in the previous paragraph are for strict compliance and it must
be ensured that no overpayments take place.
